# Contact Council

A A A

Share

Link copied

For enquiries, feedback or to report issues, there are various ways to contact Council.

## What would you like to do?

*   [Report an issue Find online forms to report issues, including road maintenance, safety hazards and unmaintained properties.](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/report-an-issue)
*   [Make a complaint Make a complaint about a noise, nuisance or dispute that’s impacting you or your neighbourhood.](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council/make-a-complaint)
*   [Dispute a fine Ask Council to review a parking or tolling fine, or an animal or environmental infringement you want to dispute.](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council/dispute-a-fine)
*   [Community engagement Have your say on matters affecting your community and Brisbane’s future. Participate in current community engagement activities and share your ideas, views and local knowledge.](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council/community-engagement)
*   [Petitions Start, sign or submit a petition to bring your concerns to Council's attention.](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council/petitions)
*   [Change your contact details Update details for your rate account, dog registration, library card or registered backflow prevention devices.](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/report-it-change-contact-details)
*   [Email Council Use this form to send general enquiries or feedback to Council.](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/email-council)

### Compliment a Council employee

We would love to hear about a positive experience you had with a Council employee. Fill out the [feedback formopens in a new tab](https://feedback.brisbane.qld.gov.au/jfe/form/SV_cx69RILtCS30iJ8 "Share a compliment form") to help us recognise outstanding service and celebrate our people. 

## How to contact Council

### ![](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/phone1.svg)By phone

Contact Council 24 hours a day, 7 days a week on [07 3403 8888](tel:0734038888 "Call Council").

Phone us for urgent issues such as:

*   lost animals
*   lost property
*   dangerous dogs
*   traffic light problems
*   public safety concerns.

We aim to answer your call within 60 seconds.

### ![](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/customer-centre1.svg)In person

Talk to Council in person at [Council’s Customer Centres](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council#Customer), which provide information and advice on a range of topics, including:

*   rates enquiries
*   animal registration
*   local laws and compliance
*   licensing, permits and applications
*   account payments (EFTPOS facilities available).

### ![](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/email.svg)By email

You can email Council using the [online formopens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/email-council "Email Council form").

If you request a Council service, we’ll provide you a reference number and details of your request within 3-5 business days.

If your request is complex or requires investigation, your email will be forwarded to the relevant business area to provide you with a written response within 30 days.

### ![](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/email.svg)By mail

Mail your letter to Council at:

Brisbane City Council    
GPO Box 1434    
Brisbane Qld 4001

We aim to provide a full response to letters within 20 working days.

### ![](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/message-alert.svg)By SMS

Use your mobile device to report a problem that needs fixing in your street or neighbourhood.

Take a photo and message details of the problem to Council on 0429 2 FIX IT ([0429 234 948](tel:0429234948 "Text Council phone number")).

Make sure to include:

*   the location
*   your name.

We aim to provide a reference number within 2 working days.

![information outline ](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/information-outline.svg/_jcr_content/renditions/original)

**Protecting your privacy is important to us**

Collecting your personal information may be necessary to complete your request and improve our services. We manage all personal information in accordance with [Council's Privacy Policy](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/governance-and-strategy/privacy-and-legal "Privacy and your right to information page").

![mdi alert yellow](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/mdi_alert_yellow.svg/_jcr_content/renditions/original)

If your enquiry is urgent, phone Council on [07 3403 8888](tel:0734038888 "Council's phone number").

## Find a Council Customer Centre

Council staff can provide information and advice on topics including:  

*   rates enquiries
*   animal registration
*   local laws and compliance
*   licensing, permits and applications
*   account payments (EFTPOS facilities available).

Map Table

[Skip map](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council#skip-map)

To activate drag with keyboard, press Alt + Enter. Once in keyboard drag state, use the arrow keys to move the marker. To complete the drag, press the Enter key. To cancel, press Escape.

## Additional services

### Relay and accessible services

If you have a hearing impairment or speech impairment, contact Council on your preferred relay call option through the National Relay Service.

[Learn moreopens in a new tab](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/about-the-nrs)

### Business Hotline

Phone 133 BNE ([133 263](tel:133263 "Business Hotline phone number")) 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for information and advice on Council’s business services, including:

*   food licensing and food safety permits
*   advertising sign advice and permits
*   Council tenders and procurement
*   development applications.

[Phone the Business Hotline](tel:133263)

### Media enquiries

For media enquiries, please contact Council via [email](mailto:Media.Matters@brisbane.qld.gov.au "Email Council").

For all other queries, please phone [07 3403 8888](tel:0734038888 "Contact Council"). University or school students are encouraged to source information for assignments from our website.

[Phone mediaopens in a new tab](tel:0403041510)

![information outline ](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/information-outline.svg/_jcr_content/renditions/original)

**Neighbourhood dispute resolution tool**

To help residents understand the most appropriate and effective next step for their situation, the Queensland Government provides an online [neighbourhood dispute resolution toolopens in a new tab](https://www.qld.gov.au/law/housing-and-neighbours/resolve-disputes "neighbourhood dispute resolution tool"), which guides users through available options, including self-resolution and other support services.

# Employee access

A A A

Share

Link copied

This page is for the use of Brisbane City Council employees only. If you’re not a Council employee, please return to the Brisbane City Council home page.

![information outline ](/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/common/icons/information-outline.svg/_jcr_content/renditions/original)

**Looking for Council jobs?**

Create an online profile in our Talent Community so we can match your skills and interests to new opportunities.

[Join our Talent Communityopens in a new tab](https://www.livehire.com/talent/community/brisbanecitycouncil/careers/contact "Livehire platform website")

## Online services

Employees can log in to quickly and easily access:

#### Email and calendar

Via a web-based version of Microsoft Outlook from any device with internet.

[Log inopens in a new tab](https://outlook.office.com/mail/)

#### Remote Access Portal

Access and use Council's remote access services. Get up-to-date information including ‘how to’ guides and tips to help you work from home. 

[Visit the Remote Access Portalopens in a new tab](https://brisbane.sharepoint.com/sites/myaccess)

#### Job opportunities

Applications from eligible Council employees will be considered for internal job opportunities. You must apply for internal job opportunities while at work and signed into Council's system (Single Sign On), or from home and remotely logged in. 

[See internal vacanciesopens in a new tab](https://brisbane.sharepoint.com/sites/jobs)

Looking for something else

[

Contact Council

](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council)[

](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council/community-engagement)[

](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council/make-a-complaint)

[Sitemap](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/governance-and-strategy/sitemap)[Contact Council](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council)

## Talent release form

Use this form if your work involves photographing or recording footage that contains Council employees or members of the public for publications, websites or social media. 

[Download the consent form opens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/consent-form-releasing-materials-council-use)

## More information

If you’re a Council employee and are having difficulties accessing these systems, please contact [Council’s ICT Service Centreopens in a new tab](https://brisbane.sharepoint.com/sites/ict-support "ICT Support - ICT Service Centre").

## Privacy statement

Council will take all reasonable and appropriate steps to protect the privacy of individuals as required by the _[Information Privacy Act 2009opens in a new tab](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-014 "Queensland Legislation website")_ (Qld) (the Act) and the Queensland Privacy Principles contained in the Act.

[

AP174 Privacy Policy

PDF  •   294 KB   •   Last modified August 2025

opens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/corpwebsite/about-council/documents/ap174-privacy-policy.pdf)

From 1 July 2026, changes to the _Information Privacy Act 2009_ (Qld) (IP Act) require local governments to comply with the Mandatory Notification Data Breach (MNDB) Scheme.

The scheme applies when there is identification or suspicion of an eligible data breach. Council has prepared the Privacy Data Breach Policy to explain how we respond and manage any data breaches. 

[

AP300 Privacy Data Breach Policy

PDF  •   193 KB   •   Last modified July 2026

opens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/corpwebsite/about-council/documents/ap300-privacy-data-breach-policy.pdf)

### Collecting your personal information

When collecting your personal information, Council will:

*   respect and protect your personal information
*   only collect what is reasonably necessary
*   only collect your personal information by lawful and fair means
*   tell you for what purpose we will be collecting the information
*   not collect sensitive information without your consent
*   tell you what information is necessary to access Council’s products and services, including payments and transactions.

### Using your personal information

When you provide Council with your personal information, Council will:

*   use the information for the purpose it was collected, unless an exception applies
*   before use, take reasonable steps to ensure the quality of the information
*   use the information to help you use Council services
*   gather the data for analysis.

### Disclosing your personal information

Council will not disclose your personal information to any other person or organisation unless:

*   you have given us your consent to do so
*   Council is required by law or authorised to do so under a law
*   there are grounds to believe disclosure will prevent a threat to life or health
*   that person or organisation is providing a service to Council and is required to maintain the same or similar privacy legislation principles
*   disclose it to external organisation, where there is a legal requirement, or when it is contracted as part of a service on Council’s behalf.

### Security of your personal information

When handling your personal information, Council will:

*   take reasonable steps to ensure that all information we collect, use or disclose is securely stored
*   monitor transmissions sent to or from Council for quality control and systems administration
*   strive to protect your personal information from misuse, interference, loss, unauthorised access, modification or disclosure
*   notify affected individuals of an identified eligible data breach (EDB).

### Accessing, correcting or updating your information

You can access and update the personal information you have given us.

In accordance with our obligations under the Act, we will take reasonable steps to correct and update your personal information if it is:

*   misleading
*   inaccurate
*   incomplete
*   out of date.

You can access any of your personal information held by Council under the [_Right to Information Act 2009_ (Qld)opens in a new tab](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-013 "Right to Information Act 2009 page on the Queensland Legislation website") and Council’s [Right to Information process](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/governance-and-strategy/privacy-and-legal#right "Right to information section of page").

You can also correct, amend or update your personal information through Council’s [change of contact detailsopens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/report-it-change-contact-details "Report it: Change your contact details form") process.

If you need any assistance with updating your information, phone Council on [07 3403 8888](tel:0734038888 "Phone Council").

### Contacting Council for privacy matters

If you think Council has breached your privacy and confidentiality, you may [contact Council](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council "Contact Council page") to alert us of the breach or lodge a complaint. We will take your complaint seriously, investigate thoroughly and provide you with a response.

To make a privacy complaint, in accordance with the _Information Privacy Act 2009_ (Qld) your complaint must:

*   be made in writing
*   provide an address in which a response can be provided
*   outline the particulars of your complaint
*   be made within 12 months after you become aware of the subject of your complaint.

If you need assistance with making your complaint, please [send an email](mailto:privacyandinformation@brisbane.qld.gov.au "Email Council") or  [Contact Council](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council "Contact Council page").

Council will respond to your privacy complaint within 45 business days after the day the complaint is received, unless an extension of time is sought.

If a response is not provided to you in this time or you are not satisfied with our response, you may make a complaint to the [Office of the Information Privacy Commissioner Queenslandopens in a new tab](https://www.oic.qld.gov.au/ "Office of the Information Privacy Commissioner Queensland website").

## Information on this website

When visiting our website, a record of your visit is logged. We do not collect personal information purely from your visit to our website.

The following data may be recorded and used by us for statistical and user experience purposes:

*   your IP address

*   your top level domain name (for example, .com, .gov, .au, .uk)

*   the type of browser you are using

*   your operating system (for example, Windows, iOS, Android, etc)

*   the date and time of your visit to the website
*   the region you are accessing the website from and its associated time zone

*   the pages accessed and the documents downloaded

*   the internet address of the website from which you were linked directly to our website.

This data is anonymised, and no attempt will be made to identify users or their browsing activities except in the unlikely event of a data breach or an investigation where a law enforcement agency or other government agency may exercise its legal authority to inspect our internet web server logs.

This website uses Google Analytics (including Display Advertising Features) and Adobe Analytics to gather anonymous information about visitors to help us monitor and improve the website. Google Analytics and Adobe Analytics each use first-party cookies and JavaScript code to gather information about how visitors use the site. For example, number of visitors, browser information, pages viewed, IP address and demographic information.

Adobe Analytics collects this information to enhance the functionality of Adobe sites and improve your experience by noting your settings and preferences. The information that Adobe Analytics collects includes website visit numbers, preferred language, country, or any other saved preference.

The information will be transmitted to and stored:

*   by Google, on servers in the United States
*   by Adobe, on servers in Australia.

This data is used by Brisbane City Council to analyse how visitors use the website in order to improve your user experience.

You can choose not to allow Google and/or Adobe to collect your information by [opting out of Google Analyticsopens in a new tab](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout "Google Analytics Opt-out Browser Add-on page on Google website"), [opting out of Google Analytics Display Advertiser Featuresopens in a new tab](https://policies.google.com/technologies/ads?gl=au "Advertising page on Google website") and/or [opting out of Adobe Productsopens in a new tab](https://www.adobe.com/au/privacy/opt-out.html#website "Adobe privacy choices page on Adobe website").

Google Tag Manager is used to deploy and manage analytics and advertising technologies including tracking pixels, which help Council understand how visitors interact with our website and digital communications. 

In addition, the website uses Facebook and Yahoo advertising Pixels to tailor content specifically for you within advertising platforms and measure the success of campaigns. Facebook and Yahoo advertising Pixels use cookies, JavaScript code, web beacons and similar technologies to gather information. No personally identifiable information is shared with us through these technologies. The information will be transmitted to and stored by the relevant provider in accordance with their privacy policies. You can choose to opt out of tailored content through the privacy settings made available by those providers.

The website uses Qualtrics intercepts to allow you to provide feedback on the website’s content and design. Qualtrics may use first-party cookies and JavaScript code to gather information about website usage including but not limited to: device and browser information, number of pages visited and time spent on the website. Qualtrics complies with applicable data privacy laws in its role as a data controller of its own data and as a data processor of customer data.

Alternatively, if you want to block cookies for all websites, you can change the privacy settings of your web browser.

In accordance with our [Privacy Policy](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/governance-and-strategy/privacy-and-legal#Privacy "Privacy Policy"), Council does not collect or keep any personally identifiable information, nor track visits to any non-Council websites.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are advised that this website may contain names, images, footage and audio of deceased persons.

### Website surveys

Sometimes Council conducts website surveys using systems developed by [Granicusopens in a new tab](https://www.granicus.com.au/ "Granicus website") and [Qualtricsopens in a new tab](https://www.qualtrics.com/en-au/ "Qualtrics website"). Data collected in these surveys is handled in accordance with Council's [Privacy Policy](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/governance-and-strategy/privacy-and-legal#Privacy "Privacy Policy").

## Right to Information

Brisbane City Council operates under the Queensland Government _[Right to Information Act 2009 opens in a new tab](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-013 "Right to Information 2009 page on the Queensland Legislation website")_[(RTI Act)opens in a new tab](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-013 "Right to Information 2009 page on the Queensland Legislation website") and the _[Information Privacy Act 2009 opens in a new tab](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-014 "Information Privacy Act 2009 page on the Queensland Legislation website")_[(IP Act)opens in a new tab](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-014 "Information Privacy Act 2009 page on the Queensland Legislation website").

Due to legislation changes, from 1 July 2025, all applications for information will be under the RTI Act. Applications for your personal information will still be free.

### Accessing Council information

Before entering the application process, check whether the information required is accessible via any of the means listed below. If the information is accessible by other means, an application under the RTI Act should not be lodged.

To check if information is already accessible, you can: 

*   view the [Publication Scheme](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/governance-and-strategy/privacy-and-legal#scheme "Council's Publication Scheme")
*   use the search function on Council's website  
    
*   [view Council's Disclosure Log](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/governance-and-strategy/privacy-and-legal#log "Council's disclosure log")  
    
*   view the list of published datasets on [Council's Open Data websiteopens in a new tab](https://www.data.brisbane.qld.gov.au/ "Council's Open Data website")  
    
*   phone Council on [07 3403 8888](tel:0734038888 "Phone Council").  
    

An application for information may be made under the RTI Act. This includes CCTV footage held by Council.

Applications under the RTI Act may be made by completing the Right to Information Application form (either online or by paper application), providing certain types of information and paying the application fee (if applicable). 

If the application form is not used, applications can be in writing, however written applications must:

*   give sufficient information concerning the document being sought to enable it to be identified
*   state an address to which notices can be sent to the applicant
*   state whether access to the document is sought for the benefit of, or use by the applicant, or another entity (and this other entity must be named)
*   if the application is for personal information of the applicant, then evidence of identity must be provided.

### Closed-Circuit Television Cameras (CCTV) requests

You can request footage from [Council’s CCTV cameras](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/community-support-and-safety/health-and-safety/safety-camera-network-closed-circuit-television-footage "Safety camera network closed circuit television footage page"). Traffic and CitySafe CCTV footage is available for a maximum of 31 calendar days from the date of recording. Bus CCTV footage is available for a maximum of 14 calendar days from the date recording.

Before requesting CCTV footage, phone Council on [07 3403 8888](tel:0734038888 "Phone Council") to check if a CCTV camera is in the location and that the footage is still available.

If you are a government agency, such as the Queensland Police Service or the Department of Transport and Main Roads, you can [request CCTV footage onlineopens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/request-for-council-cctv-footage "CCTV footage request page").

Individuals and non-government organisations can request CCTV footage by [lodging a RTI applicationopens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/right-to-information "Right to information application page").

### Lodging an application

Applicants are encouraged to apply online.

[Submit an RTI application opens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/council-services-and-requests/right-to-information)

If you’re unable, or prefer not, to submit an online application, a paper or scanned PDF format application or an application in writing can be lodged: 

*   in person at a [Council Customer Centre](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council#Customer "Contact Council page")
*   by [emailing Council](mailto:Brisbane.RTI@brisbane.qld.gov.au "Email Council")
*   by mail to:  
    

Right to Information Team  
Brisbane City Council  
GPO Box 1434  
Brisbane Qld 4001

Please refer to the table above to see if an application fee is payable for your type of application. If your application requires the application fee to be paid, you will need to complete the credit card authorisation form. Alternatively, we will contact you to arrange payment of the relevant fee.

opens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/corpwebsite/about-council/documents/right-to-information-access-application-form.pdf)

[

Credit Card Authorisation - Right to Information

PDF  •   85 KB   •   Last modified July 2025

opens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/content/dam/brisbanecitycouncil/corpwebsite/about-council/documents/credit-card-authorisation-right-to-information.pdf)

Where evidence of identity is required to be lodged with an access application, applicants must provide one of the following:

*   a certified copy of a current driver's licence
*   a certified copy of the identifying page of a current passport
*   a certified copy of a birth certificate
*   a certified statutory declaration from an individual who has known the applicant for at least one year
*   a copy of a prisoner's identity card certified by a corrective services officer
*   an electronic PDF document of a Digital ID created using the approved app under the _Transport Planning and Coordination Act 1994_.

Alternatively, evidence of identity may be sighted by a Council officer at a Council Customer Centre. Applicants may present either:

*   an accepted form of identification; or
*   a Digital ID displayed in the approved app under the _Transport Planning and Coordination Act 1994_. 

Applications will be acknowledged by the RTI team and decision timeframes confirmed when all relevant information is provided.

### Decision reviews

If you’re dissatisfied with the officer’s decision, you can apply for

Learn how we make our website accessible to as many people as possible.

## Our commitment

Council is committed to delivering technology that enables equitable access to information and services for all users.

This commitment supports our vision for an [inclusive Brisbane](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/community-support-and-safety/support-for-community/inclusive-brisbane "Inclusive Brisbane page").  

## Web Content Accessibility Guidelines  

The [Web Content Accessibility Guidelinesopens in a new tab](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/ "WCAG 2 Overview on the W3C website") (WCAG) define internationally recognised practices for improving accessibility. These guidelines describe different levels of accessibility outcomes to support a broad range of user needs.

Council considers these guidelines in the design, development and maintenance of its website. Accessibility practices are incorporated to support usability and access for a wide range of users.

We aim to apply accessibility practices to support compatibility with assistive technologies, such as screen readers, and to improve usability for a wide range of users. Accessibility is reviewed and enhanced over time as part of ongoing improvements.

## File formats 

We aim to make downloadable content available in formats that are broadly accessible.

Some documents, however, such as scanned or archival files, cannot be made fully accessible. If you require any information on the site in an alternative format, [contact Council](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/about-council/contact-council "Contact Council page").  

## Website feedback  

If you experience any accessibility problems with our website, or with any of the information or documents, let us know by completing the [website feedback formopens in a new tab](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/online-services/report-an-issue/report-it-website-feedback "Website feedback online form ").

description:
As a not-for-profit organisation, RISING relies on support from donors, public partners and corporate organisations to help fund ambitious art and reach new audiences.

With their support, we can offer free experiences, keep our ticket prices accessible, and have a positive impact on artists, audiences, and our city.

Funding makes it possible for us to amplify voices in our community. We do this by commissioning thoughtful and challenging work, and creating pathways and infrastructure for artists to scale up their practice and mount work at a major festival.

# Partners

### [**Partner with RISING  
**](https://rising.melbourne/about/partners#partner-with-rising)

RISING is Australia’s leading contemporary arts festival, bringing bold, new art, music, and performance into the heart of Melbourne each June.  

RISING gives brands a platform to show up in culture in ways that feel relevant and memorable. From major activations and product launches to hospitality, storytelling and city-wide visibility, each partnership is built to feel distinctive and integrated into the festival.

  
We work collaboratively with our partners to achieve key business objectives, building mutually beneficial relationships that connect commercial ambition with the creative possibilities RISING can offer.  

As a not-for-profit organisation, our partners help bring ambitious work to life and make extraordinary cultural experiences accessible to more people.  

  
**BECOME A PARTNER**  
Discover how your organisation can become a part of RISING. Explore our partnerships prospectus for an introduction to the opportunities available, or get in touch with our team to discuss how we can work together.  
  
[**Contact the RISING Partnerships team**](mailto:partnerships@rising.melbourne "partnerships@rising.melbourne")  

[Explore our 2027 Partnership Prospectus](https://pitch.com/v/rising-partnership-prospectus-wrpz8v)

### 

Due Diligence

**Q. What due diligence does RISING undertake with its partners?**

A. All funding partners undergo a due diligence review of publicly available information on the prospective partner’s environmental social and governance activity to ensure they’re aligned with RISING and if applicable, the artist or program item the partnership is associated with. Any support received must also align with [RISING’s Fundraising Policy](https://static.rising.melbourne/media/Policies/29-Fundraising-Partnerships-Policy.pdf), as well RISING’s pledge for Fossil Free Sponsorship in partnership with 350 Australia. We also use external resources like the United Nations Digital Library to further research any prospective funding partners. RISING and its Board remain committed to the Fundraising Policy and will use this to guide all future prospective partnerships.

**Q. Do RISING’s funding partners influence curatorial decisions of the festival?**  
A. Curatorial decisions at RISING are made by its professional curators. No external party has influence over RISING’s curators or their curatorial decisions, and any partner contribution—in-kind, financial or otherwise—that aims to restrict or impede the work of RISING, its curators or artists in the program is rejected.

RISING is a festival aspiring to be a cultural leader in inclusion and access. We want our organisation and program to be a true reflection of our city representing people with a variety of skillsets and life experiences, cultures and backgrounds.

We encourage applications from First Nations people, those who are from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people who are LGBTQIA+, Neurodivergent people, people with a disability and/or who are d/Deaf.

If you have any questions regarding job opportunities you can ask them at [jobs@rising.melbourne](mailto:jobs@rising.melbourne "jobs@rising.melbourne").

If you have any questions about access, including about reasonable adjustments, you can ask them confidentially at [access@rising.melbourne](mailto:access@rising.melbourne "access@rising.melbourne") or call us on 03 9662 4242.

## [SENIOR DESIGNER](https://rising.melbourne/about/jobs#undefined)

### MIXED PART-TIME/FULL TIME, FIXED TERM UNTIL JUNE 2027

Closing date : Sun, Nov 8, 2026

The Senior Designer oversees and leads the visual brand for the festival and its sub-brands and ensures its smooth execution across all brand touchpoints. The role is suited to a proactive and conceptual thinker with a wide breadth of creative campaign experience, who is comfortable managing briefs and other designers’ workloads, as well as balancing competing priorities.

Please provide a cover letter, resume and a link to your portfolio. We will be conducting rolling interviews as we receive applications. Final applications close 11.59pm, Sun 8 November 2026.

# People

## [Artistic Director and CEO](https://rising.melbourne/about/people#artistic-director-and-ceo)

### Hannah Fox

Artistic Director and CEO

Hannah is an artist, curator and festival director with a focus on sound art, large-scale public art, contemporary music and live art. Prior to her role as RISING Artistic Director, Hannah worked as Artistic Associate at Melbourne Festival; and as the Associate Creative Director of Dark Mofo.

Her broad spectrum of work has included performance interventions for the Tate Modern, a Janes Addiction stage show, and choreographing cranes and forklifts for a large-scale car stunt show. She’s a founding member of the creative partnership Supple Fox, which currently collaborates with artist Byron J Scullin on work including the large-scale, outdoor sonic artwork Siren Song, which continues to be remounted in cities around the world.

## [Curators](https://rising.melbourne/about/people#curators)

### Kimberley Moulton

SENIOR CURATOR, EXHIBITIONS

Dr Kimberley Moulton is a Yorta Yorta woman and an independent curator and writer. She is Senior Curator Exhibitions at RISING and recently held tenure as the Adjunct Curator Indigenous Art for Tate, London (2023-2026). Kimberley was previously Senior Curator First Peoples Collection at Museums Victoria. Her recent exhibitions include the Tarrawarra Biennial : We Are Eagles (2025), On Country: Photography from Australia (Les Rencontres d'Arles France, co-curated, 2025), Emily Kam Kngwarray (Tate Modern, curatorial team, 2025), The Blak Infinite (co-curated, 2024) and Shadow Spirit (RISING, 2023). She has published extensively on contemporary Indigenous art, collections and curatorial practice. Kimberley works at the intersection of historical collections and contemporary art and her practice aims to extend what exhibitions, public art and research can be for First Peoples communities and artists globally. She holds a PhD in Curatorial Practice, Monash University and is an Emeritus Curator with Museums Victoria. In 2025 she was recipient of the Sidney Myer Creative Fellowship.

### Hayley Percy

SENIOR CURATOR, MUSIC

Hayley Percy is a Wiradjuri woman living and working in Naarm/Melbourne. Hayley has twenty years of varied professional experience across the music and entertainment industry with a strong background in large high impact public events, music festivals as well as large scale project management. Additional to her current role as Senior Curator, Music for RISING festival, Hayley is also the Executive Producer and Co-Director of Blaktasia, Australia's first Aboriginal mobile game. 

Her background in major events has afforded her a vast network within the music, media, promotional and sponsorship landscape and she has a broad skill set in ensuring high impact launches of products and events alike.

### Kate ten Buuren

FIRST PEOPLES MELBOURNE ART TRAMS CURATOR

Kate is a Taungurung artist, curator, and a founding member of the collective this mob. Interested in contemporary visual art, film and stories, Kate grounds her practice in self-determination, self-representation and collectivism. Earlier this year, she curated the Telstra National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Awards in Darwin, and in 2024 she co-curated The Blak Infinite for RISING Melbourne.

## [Board of Directors](https://rising.melbourne/about/people#board-of-directors)

### Simon Phemister, PSM

CHAIR

Simon Phemister is the Founder and Managing Partner of Frank Partners, a strategic advisory firm focused on bridging government and industry to deliver high-impact outcomes. He has held senior roles in both public and private sectors, including as Secretary of the Department of Jobs, Precincts and Regions, where he led reforms in housing, land use, and economic development. Simon is also a founding partner of the Dux Project and previously a Partner at EY Port Jackson Partners. With a career spanning policy, strategy, and major event delivery—including the Australian Open and Formula 1 Grand Prix—he brings deep expertise in public-private collaboration and a passion for building Victoria’s economy.

### David Vodicka

David is the founder of Media Arts Lawyers where he represents high-profile musicians, celebrities and entertainment companies. He chairs the board of Australian Independent Record Labels Association, is a board member of Australian Recording Industry Association and the Phonographic Performance Company of Australia. He was previously a board member of the Melbourne International Film Festival.

### Liz Dax

Elizabeth M. Dax AM is a director and board chair with a focus on governance, finance, and risk in the not-for-profit sector. Formerly Director of Australia’s National Reference Laboratory, she has held leadership roles in national and international HIV/AIDS organizations. A physician and scientist, she also led a WHO Collaborating Centre on virus diagnostics.

### Vicky Zaparas

Vicky Zaparas is the founder of Vicky Zaparas Interiors, exhibiting at the National Gallery of Victoria. Formerly Brand Manager at The Body Shop Australia, she helped establish the Hellenic Museum Ladies Society and is an Australian Ballet Ambassador. With expertise in design, fashion, and marketing, she champions Victoria’s creative industries on a global stage.

### Martin Foley

Martin Foley sits on a number of creative sector Boards bringing his experience as a senior Minister in the Victorian Government to assist organisations, communities, creatives and governments to deliver artistic, creative, social and economic value. He also works across a number of health and social care areas. He joined the RISING Board in 2023.

### Kerri Turner

Kerri is a partner at Ernst & Young and focuses on providing CFO advisory services. Kerri has a keen interest in the arts and supporting various community activities in Melbourne. She has served on the boards for Malthouse Theatre board and the Centre for Contemporary Photography.

### Brad Jenkins

Brad is a CEO and Board Director with over 30 years’ experience working across Victorian events, venues, and member-based organisations. He’s the Chief Executive of Melbourne Royal, where he leads the team behind the iconic Melbourne Royal Show and oversees Melbourne Showgrounds—Victoria’s largest indoor-outdoor venue for events, festivals, and exhibitions. He also runs a calendar of events and awards celebrating excellence in food, drink, and agriculture.

# Contact

### 

Office Hours

Monday—Friday, 11am—4pm

### 

Where to find us

**Office**

Level 2, 377 Lonsdale Street

Melbourne VIC 3000

Australia

**Postal Address**

PO BOX 10

Flinders Lane VIC 8009

Australia

### 

General Enquiries

For general enquiries, call us on 03 9662 4242 or email [hello@rising.melbourne](mailto:hello@rising.melbourne "hello@rising.melbourne").

For ticketing enquiries, please email us at [ticketing@rising.melbourne](mailto:ticketing@rising.melbourne "ticketing@rising.melbourne"). If you require access services, please call 03 9662 4242 and follow the prompts to leave a voicemail. Our team will call you back to assist with your request.

### 

Media

For media enquiries, contact [Jadan](mailto:jadan@commonstate.co "jadan@commonstate.co"). Here's our [media centre](https://media.commonstate.co/rising-2026/), too.

### 

Partnerships

For partnership opportunities, contact [our partnerships team](mailto:partnerships@rising.melbourne "partnerships@rising.melbourne").

### 

Donate

To make a donation, drop our [donation inbox](mailto:donate@rising.melbourne "donate@rising.melbourne") a line or visit the [Support page](https://rising.melbourne/support-and-donate).

### 

Feedback

We hope you have a great experience at RISING. If you have thoughts on what we can improve, please send us an email at [hello@rising.melbourne](mailto:hello@rising.melbourne "hello@rising.melbourne") or via mail to PO Box 10, Flinders Lane, Victoria 8009. We’ll respond in writing within 48 business hours of receipt.

# Gift Vouchers

## [Tickets vouchers](https://rising.melbourne/about/general-faqs/gift-vouchers#tickets-vouchers)

Moon Units are RISING’s official currency for tickets. Vouchers are available to purchase online or over the phone and have an expiry of 3 years from date of purchase. Recipients can redeem Moon Units for tickets purchased via the RISING website.

[Buy a ticket voucher here](https://tickets.rising.melbourne/moon-units)

## [Merchandise vouchers](https://rising.melbourne/about/general-faqs/gift-vouchers#merchandise-vouchers)

Seeking out a gift or memento for a fellow stargazer? Give a RISING merch voucher. They can be exchanged for all sorts of goodies and artist collab merchandise.

[Buy a merch voucher here](https://shop.rising.melbourne/products/rising-merch-gift-voucher)

# Call to Artists

RISING's Call to Artists program is an open invitation to artists to submit their ideas for bold, ambitious new work.

The Call to Artists was launched in May 2020, in the midst of the pandemic, as a way to support artists and cultivate works for RISING's future festival programming while in lockdown.

The call resulted in several works being commissioned for the 2021, 2022 and 2023 festivals.

The last Call to Artists happened in June/July 2022, which will see works commissioned for 2024 and beyond.

Please note: RISING is not currently accepting submissions.

# FAQs

For any questions not answered below, head to the [contact page](https://rising.melbourne/about/contact) to find the right person to answer your enquiry.

### 

Q. What is RISING?

A. RISING is Victoria's flagship festival of new art, music, performance held in June each year in the heart of Naarm/Melbourne.

### 

Q. I’m not sure if RISING is for me. What kind of events will be in the program?

A. RISING is for everyone. From visual art, performance and public art installations to live music and parties, we have all kinds of experiences for you to enjoy whatever you’re into.

### 

Q. I would like to volunteer, intern or work for RISING. How do I apply?

A. Thank you for your interest! We advertise employment opportunities on our [Jobs](https://rising.melbourne/jobs) page and will be advertising any volunteering opportunities on our social channels (follow us on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/rising.melbourne/), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/risingmelb/), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/rising-melbourne), and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@rising.melbourne), and via email ([subscribe here](https://rising.melbourne/subscribe)).

### 

Q. I’m an artist who’s keen to be part of RISING. How can I submit my work and ideas for consideration?

A. RISING prides itself on commissioning Australian and particularly First Nations and Victorian work to be programmed alongside our international offerings. We do regular artist callouts through our newsletter and social channels. [Subscribe](https://rising.melbourne/subscribe) and follow to stay updated.

### 

Q. I'm a photographer/videographer. Can I shoot for RISING?

A. Thanks for your interest. We have a number of photographers and videographers that we currently work with. If you would like to be considered for our roster, please send through a link to your folio and your day rate to hello@rising.melbourne. Please note that you may not receive a response from us. If you're interested in shooting on behalf of a media publication or yourself, please contact our publicists at Common State.

BOOKING & PRICING

### 

How do I book?

Browse the program to see our full 2026 offering online. All listings are being updated to reflect the most recent information. ​

​The best way to book tickets is via the RISING website, simply click the BUY TICKETS button on the page of the show/event you'd like to attend. ​ ​

You can email us at [ticketing@rising.melbourne](mailto:ticketing@rising.melbourne) for any queries. Please note that the team cannot accept your credit card information via email, but they can answer any questions you have and can follow up purchase enquiries via phone.

### 

Can I book in person?

Tickets can be booked via the RISING website by clicking the 'Buy Tickets' button on the page of the show/event you’d like to attend.

If you require access services, please call the customer service line on (03) 9653 8620 and leave a voicemail. One of our team will call you back to assist with your request.

### 

How much are tickets?

For more information about price types, [click here](https://rising.melbourne/about/general-faqs/pricing)

### 

Do I qualify for a concession or discounted ticket price?

If you hold any of the following, you’re eligible for a concession priced ticket. Please come prepared to show your proof of concession with your ticket at the venue.

— Full-Time Students (incl. international students)

— Children under 16 years of age

— MEAA Members

— Victorian Carer Card holders

— Government issued Health Care Card holders

— Pensioners

— Seniors Card holders

We also offer discounted tickets for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander community members.

### 

What is Early Bird and First Release pricing?

Early Bird is a discount exclusively available during our subscriber presale period. It offers 20% off select shows across the program. Early Bird tickets are limited and available during presale or until allocation exhausts.

Release pricing is available for some events in our music program. Some events are sold in release tiers, where prices increase as allocations sell out.

### 

How do I use the discount/promo code?

Congratulations on getting a code! After “buy tickets” and just before selecting the ticket dates and times, there is a box to "enter a promo code". A pop up will confirm a successful application. Now you can choose the unlocked ticket type and add them to your cart.

### 

Are there discounts for the Australian Dance Biennale?

This package offers a 15% discount on tickets when purchasing three or more Australian Dance Biennale events. This offer is subject to availability, and applicable to Standard tickets for General Admission events, and Standard A-Reserve tickets for allocated seating events. Click [here](https://rising.melbourne/program?filters={%22category%22:[%22Dance+Biennale%22]}) to see all Dance Biennale Events

### 

How do I make a group booking?

Some of our events may have a discounted group price—the size of the group required to access the price will be listed on the event page.

For groups greater than 10 people, please submit an enquiry by emailing groups@rising.melbourne and we’ll get in touch as soon as possible.

### 

How do I sign up for an Art Pass?

A RISING thank you to all the people who make the art happen in our city. To sign up and find deals for an Art Pass, click [here](https://rising.melbourne/about/general-faqs/art-pass)

### 

Can I buy a gift voucher?

Yes! You can buy a gift voucher [here](https://rising.melbourne/about/general-faqs/gift-vouchers). Voucher can be used only for tickets purchased directly through RISING (not through a partner ticket seller such as Ticketek, Ticketmaster or one of our venue partners) and are valid for 3 years from the date of purchase.

### 

What are your terms and conditions of sale?

Tickets are non-refundable except as required by law, in accordance with the Live Performance Australia (LPA) Ticketing Code of Practice.

All tickets are sold subject to our terms and conditions of sale. You can also access our Privacy Policy.

TICKETS & ORDERS

### 

Why haven't I received my confirmation email?

You may have entered your email address incorrectly at checkout, please email us at [ticketing@rising.melbourne](mailto:ticketing@rising.melbourne) with any order information you have and the customer experience team will investigate for you.

### 

I've been issued a ticket from someone other than RISING, is it legit?

Some of our venues will also be issuing tickets for RISING events. Currently, the authorised ticket sellers for RISING are:

Arts Centre Melbourne, ACMI, Malthouse Theatre, Melbourne Recital Centre, Melbourne Theatre Company, OzTix, Ticketmaster, and Ticketek.

### 

Why are my tickets locked?

Digital tickets can be accessed in your confirmation email via the tickets link. As an added protection against scalping, we have locked tickets until 48 hours prior to the perfomance.

We’ll send a reminder and any important event information to the email address you book with. So make sure it’s one you regularly check and can access on the go.

### 

Can I get a printed ticket posted to me?

As part of our sustainability practices, we don’t post tickets. Digital tickets replace our printed tickets and are made available 48 hours before your event. If you’re unable to access digital tickets, you can contact our customer service team via email at [ticketing@rising.melbourne](mailto:ticketing@rising.melbourne)

TICKET CHANGES

### 

Can I exchange my ticket?

Exchanges are possible, and are subject to availability and a $3 per-ticket exchange fee. Requests must be made at least 24 hours prior to the event.

For us to look into exchanging your ticket(s), fill out our [exchange request form](https://risingmelbourne.fillout.com/exchange-request-form), and a member from our team will get back to you.

### 

Can I transfer my tickets to someone else?

Yes, if you cannot go to an event, you can pass your tickets onto your friends or family. A name change or email transfer is not required. Simply send a screenshot of the ticket QR code when they unlock 48 hours before the event.

Please note, we do not recommend sending the entire ticket link as this will give them access to all RISING tickets under your account.  

### 

Can I get a refund?

Unfortunately, it’s not possible for RISING to refund completed bookings, except as required by law or in accordance with the [LPA Ticketing Code of Conduct](https://liveperformance.com.au/resources/?type=919).

We recommend you pass on the tickets to your friends and family or you can resell them with Tixel.

### 

How do I resell my ticket?

RISING has partnered with [Tixel](https://tixel.com/au/festival-tickets/rising-tickets) to assist festival goers with their ticket resale.

Tixel is a safe and transparent event marketplace that allows fans to easily exchange tickets at a fair price. Every ticket is verified and prices are capped to protect fans from scalpers and scams.

To list your tickets:

1\. Go to [https://tixel.com/sell/email](https://tixel.com/sell/email)

2\. Forward your RISING Order Confirmation to the generated Tixel email address

3\. Once you have forwarded the email, select 'I've forwarded my ticket'. This may take a few minutes to process.

4\. When verification is complete, you will need to toggle the 'sell this ticket' option for each ticket you need to list for sale, and continue to adjust the listing price.

Since our tickets are locked until 48 hours prior to the performance, you will need to send them manually when they unlock. When somebody purchases your tickets:

5\. Hop into the buyer/seller chat and let them know you'll upload the tickets as soon as they're available.

6\. Once the QR code unlocks, screenshot and send them, via your chat, to the buyer

That's it! If there are further queries, you can view Tixel's very helpful FAQ and Help Centre resource

title: RISING: Partners
description:
As a not-for-profit organisation, RISING relies on support from donors, public partners and corporate organisations to help fund ambitious art and reach new audiences.

With their support, we can offer free experiences, keep our ticket prices accessible, and have a positive impact on artists, audiences, and our city.

Funding makes it possible for us to amplify voices in our community. We do this by commissioning thoughtful and challenging work, and creating pathways and infrastructure for artists to scale up their practice and mount work at a major festival.

# Partners

### [**Partner with RISING  
**](https://rising.melbourne/about/partners#partner-with-rising)

RISING is Australia’s leading contemporary arts festival, bringing bold, new art, music, and performance into the heart of Melbourne each June.  

RISING gives brands a platform to show up in culture in ways that feel relevant and memorable. From major activations and product launches to hospitality, storytelling and city-wide visibility, each partnership is built to feel distinctive and integrated into the festival.

  
We work collaboratively with our partners to achieve key business objectives, building mutually beneficial relationships that connect commercial ambition with the creative possibilities RISING can offer.  

As a not-for-profit organisation, our partners help bring ambitious work to life and make extraordinary cultural experiences accessible to more people.  

  
**BECOME A PARTNER**  
Discover how your organisation can become a part of RISING. Explore our partnerships prospectus for an introduction to the opportunities available, or get in touch with our team to discuss how we can work together.  
  
[**Contact the RISING Partnerships team**](mailto:partnerships@rising.melbourne "partnerships@rising.melbourne")  

[Explore our 2027 Partnership Prospectus](https://pitch.com/v/rising-partnership-prospectus-wrpz8v)

### 

Due Diligence

**Q. What due diligence does RISING undertake with its partners?**

A. All funding partners undergo a due diligence review of publicly available information on the prospective partner’s environmental social and governance activity to ensure they’re aligned with RISING and if applicable, the artist or program item the partnership is associated with. Any support received must also align with [RISING’s Fundraising Policy](https://static.rising.melbourne/media/Policies/29-Fundraising-Partnerships-Policy.pdf), as well RISING’s pledge for Fossil Free Sponsorship in partnership with 350 Australia. We also use external resources like the United Nations Digital Library to further research any prospective funding partners. RISING and its Board remain committed to the Fundraising Policy and will use this to guide all future prospective partnerships.

**Q. Do RISING’s funding partners influence curatorial decisions of the festival?**  
A. Curatorial decisions at RISING are made by its professional curators. No external party has influence over RISING’s curators or their curatorial decisions, and any partner contribution—in-kind, financial or otherwise—that aims to restrict or impede the work of RISING, its curators or artists in the program is rejected.

**Got questions about RISING and how it's funded? Please get in touch via** **[feedback@rising.melbourne](mailto:feedback@rising.melbourne "feedback@rising.melbourne").**

### **Welcome to Blazing Swan 2026, Takes a Village**

The Blazing Swan annual event is dedicated to RADICAL SELF-EXPRESSION and RADICAL SELF-RELIANCE for seven days of community over the Easter Long Weekend, from Wednesday 1st April 2026 (noon) to Tuesday 7th April 2026 (noon)

Blazing Swan is an official Burning Man Regional Event. We practice DECOMMODIFICATION, placing ourselves and our relationships at the centre of our own lives, GIVING and receiving openly, being IMMEDIATELY present, and acknowledging that everything we have ever accomplished, everything we will ever accomplish, only happens through COMMUNAL EFFORT. We will be RADICALLY EXPRESSIVE and RADICALLY INCLUSIVE and ask only of ourselves and others that we respect and value each other and practice kindness and caring. Blazing Swan is not a spectator event. Every participant is a performer, every act is a performance. Find your best self, your creative self, and play it out on the stage that is Blazing Swan.

Blazing Swan gives absolute priority to CONSENT, CIVIC RESPONSIBILITY and LEAVING NO TRACE. When you purchase a ticket you sign-up to say you understand what all these things mean, and you will follow our rules which are there to keep everyone safe. People do ask, “Why do you have so many rules? More than any other event I’ve ever been to!” It’s because we care. And a week in the Australian outback is not a naturally safe space. Be prepared. Read the Ticket FAQ and the Event FAQ on the Website, read the Survival Guide, read about the Principles and our Statement of Inclusion. Get your head around our Blazing Swan Tickets and Event Attendance Terms and Conditions. PARTICIPATION and CIVIC RESPONSIBILITY starts here.

Special thanks to Timmy Howe for this year’s beautiful artwork.

### Need to know more about Blazing Swan 2026, Takes A Village ?

One of our 11 Principles is ‘Radical Self Reliance’.  This means that if you want to know more about Takes A Village, if you want to prepare for Takes A Village, and if you want to have your best possibe time at Takes A Village – make an effort!  Just getting out to the event site and literally surviving will require you to make an effort.  Blazing Swan Takes A Village is not meant to be easy.  It is intentionally challenging.  Come join us and survive and thrive – and be your best, kindest and most authentic self!

If you want to know more about Blazing Swan Takes A Village go and talk with someone who has been to a Blazing Swan Event, connect up with our [social media](https://www.facebook.com/groups/OfficialBlazingSwanCommunity), and then:

*   read our [Acknowledgement of Country page](https://blazingswan.com.au/acknowledgement-of-country/)
*   read about our [11 Principles page](https://blazingswan.com.au/11-principles/)
*   read our [Short History of Blazing Swan page](https://blazingswan.com.au/blazing-swan-a-short-history/)
*   read our [Event FAQ page](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/)
*   read our [Ticket FAQ page](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/)
*   read our [Event Survival Guides](https://blazingswan.com.au/survival-guide/)

*   if you are interested in Theme Camps read our [Theme Camps Information page](https://blazingswan.com.au/theme-camp-information/)
*   if you are interested in Arts at Takes A Village read our [Arts page](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-applications/)
*   if you are interested in Volunteering, read our [Volunteering page](https://blazingswan.com.au/volunteering/)  
    

### What about  tickets for Takes A Village ?

You will need to purchase a ticket.   Volunteers, Theme Camp crew, Artist and Mutant Vehicle crew and Association Members will all be contacted separately about tickets.

When you enter the Event site with a ticket you must accept the conditions that go along with that ticket, including our right to refuse you entry or to require you to leave the Event site if you do not comply with those conditions.  We do this to keep everyone safe and we take this responsibility very seriously.

### What Dates should I watch out for ?

*   Applications for funding and registration of artworks at Takes A Village are closed.
*   Applications to volunteer with Blazing Swan in year-round roles are [always open](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vQlEgvUPdglOQbLRaA1BcbwlKHx8FuveoUODy7EOif1hFlbBrQudV_9qNdb5XwsdbcV1lacKcqI_Max/pub)
*   The second (and final) round of Applications to bring a Theme Camp to Takes A Village have closed.
*   Applications to bring a Mutant Vehicle to Takes A Village have closed, but you can still register an accessibility vehicle
*   Tickets for Theme Camps, Artists and Mutant Vehicle operators will be allocated once they have applied for registration AND been accepted.
*   Tickets for Event specific Volunteers will be allocated AFTER the volunteer has applied AND been accepted.  These tickets may be cancelled by us if the volunteer does not meet specific requirements such as attending (in person or online) training sessions prior to the Event

### What else should I know ?

You’ll find the answers to almost everything if you follow the leads we’ve given to you on this page.  IF you have looked down all those rabbit holes and STILL can’t find the answer you’re looking for, feel free to contact us.   We’ll wrap up this page with three special reminders:

**One.**  Our Blazing Swan Event is subject to all State Laws and regulations.  This is consistent with our Principle of Civic Responsibility.  Police can and will patrol the Event site.   Blazing Swan will not encourage any activity that breaches the law and we will comply, and require our attendees to comply, with all relevant Health and Safety regulations.

**Two.**  Blazing Swan takes Consent very seriously.  It is one of our Principles, and it is an absolute requirement of all our Event attendees.

**Three.**  Blazing Swan is not just an Event that happens out in the ‘bush’.  We see the Kulin, Njaki Njaki and Wheatbelt communities as our special friends and allies.  We have been invited into these communites and we hope that all of our Event participants will see not just the magic in our Event, but also the magic in these modern and ancient communities.

# Blazing Swan Ticket FAQ

Got questions? We've got answers.

# Your Name on the Ticket MUST Match Your ID

If they do not match, you will be refused entry to the event

## Tickets FAQ

### [How many tickets can I buy?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

You can purchase a maximum of 2 Adult tickets in any one transaction.  You MUST specify the names of the people who are going to go through the Gate with each of those tickets.  You CAN NOT use your own name twice on those tickets.  One of those two tickets will be invalid.

After you purchase your Adult ticket you can contact Blazing Swan if you need additional tickets for Children or Carers.

To contact Blazing Swan, use the ‘Contact Host’ option on the Humanitix Blazing Swan Event page.

### [Can I buy tickets for my Children?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

Yes.  If you are purchasing an Adult you will see an option in Humanitix to purchase tickets for your children as well.

Tickets for Children between 12 and 17 years of age are $100 each.  Tickets for Children under 12 are free, but they MUST have a ticket or they will not be admitted to the Event.

Blazing Swan is an all ages event. Anyone under 18 years old must be under the supervision of their parent or legal guardian at all times.  Blazing Swan will provide anyone under 18 with a special wristband which must not be removed or defaced for the duration of the Event.

Any person under 18 attempting to obtain alcohol, and any person under 18 drinking alcohol, may be asked to leave the event along with their parents or guardians and siblings.

There are some Adult themed areas and activities at Blazing Swan.  These will be signposted and described as such in our ‘Where’s the Fun’ guide book.  Under 18’s are not permitteed to enter into these areas or partake in these activities.

### [I am under 18 years of age, can I buy a ticket?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

NO.  All under 18 and under 12 tickets can only be purchased WITH an adult ticket purchased by the parent or legal guardian.

### [My Child turns 12 or 18 during the Event, do I need to pay more?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

NO.  The Ticket Type and price is set according to how old your Child is on the first day of the event – even if you didn’t come through the Gate on that date.  Whatever you paid is good for the seven days.

HOWEVER, any child turning 18 during the Event will need to have Blazing Swan replace their Children Wristband with a properly issued Adult Wristband on the appropriate day.  Parents/Guardians can contact a Ranger or Centre Kiosk to get someone to help them.

And Happy Birthday – in advance !

### [I am disabled and need to come with a carer. Can I get a ticket for them?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

If you are disabled and have purchased an Adult ticket you can contact Blazing Swan and talk with us about purchasing additional tickets for your eligible carer.  We will talk through some things with you and once we have established eligibility we will send you a code that you can use to purchase Carer’s tickets from Humanitix.

Depending on the nature of the care relationship your carer might receive their ticket for free – but they will still need a ticket.  Blazing Swan follows WA State Government advice in identifying Carers who are eligible for free tickets.  Please contact us to discuss your situation.

To contact Blazing Swan, use the ‘Contact Host’ option on the Humanitix Blazing Swan Event page and briefly explain what you need.

### [Can I buy tickets at the Event Gate?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

NO.  There are no Gate Ticket Sales.  Our Gate does not handle or keep cash.

### [Will tickets sell out?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

Some years the first round of Blazing Swan tickets have sold out in a couple of hours.

### [I have been accepted as a volunteer, do I need to puchase a ticket?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

If you have been accepted as a volunteer and have attended and performed satisfactorily in our training you will be offered a Volunteer Ticket.  This ticket will be issued in your name and it can not be sold or transferred except back to Blazing Swan.

If you are a volunteer and plan on attending our Event with a partner who is NOT volunteering, your partner(s) will need to purchase a Ticket at the regular price.   We can not guarantee that such a ticket will be available at the time you attempt to make that purchase.  We recommend that the partner(s) of volunteers also apply to volunteer with us.

If you are a volunteer and plan to bring your under 18 children please contact your Team Lead or the Volunteer Manager.  Please note that children under the age of 18 are not permitted on the Event site prior to Event opening or after Event closing.

### [I am a Theme Camp crew member, Art Work crew member, Mutant Vehicle crew member or Blazing Swan Association Member, do i need to purchase a ticket?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

If you are a registered crew member of a Theme Camp or Art Work or Mutant Vehicle that is registered with Blazing Swan, or a Blazing Swan Association Member on the date that the First Ticket Round opens, you will be offered a Ticket at a discount to the regular price.  This ticket will be issued in your name and it can not be sold or transferred except back to Blazing Swan.

If you are offered a Ticket in any of these categories and your partner(s) is not, your partner(s) will need to purchase a Ticket at the regular price.   We can not guarantee that such a ticket will be available at the time you attempt to make that purchase.  We recommend in these cases that your partner consider volunteering with us.

If you are a Theme Camp crew member you might want to consider volunteering with us AS WELL.  This way you could be eligible for a volunteering ticket which takes the pressure off your Theme Camp to find scarce Theme Camps tickets.  Talk to your Theme Camp Lead about this option.

If you are offered a Ticket in any of thes categories and you plan to bring your under 18 children please contact Blazing Swan.  Please note that children under the age of 18 are not permitted on the Event worksite prior to Event opening at noon on Wednesday 1st April 2026, or after Event closing at noon on Tuesday 7th April 2026.

### [What else can I do to get a ticket?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

At this late stage, unless you are a local Kulin resident, there is no possibility of obtaining a ticket to the Blazing Swan event.  It is fully sold out and all volunteer positions have been filled.  We look forward to seeing you NEXT year.

### [Are there any discounts?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

Regular and Children Ticket prices are as posted on this website.   Association Members along with Approved Volunteers, Theme Camp members, Mutant Vehicle Operators and Art Team crew are offered tickets at a rate below the Regular Ticket price.

Tickets are priced to cover expenses and all surplus monies are returned to fund future Blazing Swan Events and other activities consistent with our Constitution.  Blazing Swan in a Not-for-Profit organisation.

We do not offer free tickets if it is your birthday during the event.  But we will celebrate it with you !

### [Can I buy a ticket just for the weekend?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

NO.  Everyone purchases a ticket for the full Event period.  Attendees may arrive anytime or anyday after the Event Gate opens at noon on Wednesday 1st April 2026.  If you arrive late in the evening you will be required to park your vehicle in a holding area and drive up to your camp site the next morning.  Unless given specific permission, all attendees must leave the Event site by noon on Tuesday 7th April 2026.

We strongly recommend that drivers have an ‘easy night’ on Monday and get a good sleep so they are at their very best on the Tuesday.

### [I'm a Kulin local, is there something for me?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

Absolutely.  Blazing Swan loves Kulin and traditionally invites local residents to join us for the burning of our Effigy and the light show on Saturday evening.   Day passes – for that Saturday only – will be organised through the Shire, as they are every year, and available closer to the event date.   The Shire will let locals know when that’s happening.

Note that people entering the Event with a pass provided by the Kulin Shire will be bound by the [Blazing Swan Event Attendance and Tickets Terms and Conditions](https://blazingswan.com.au/terms-conditions/), a copy of which will be available at the venue where the passes are being handed out.  Prices for the day passes are set by the Shire.

### [I can no longer attend, how do I resell or transfer my ticket?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

If you can no longer attend this event, and you purchased your ticket in a public sale,  contact Blazing Swan at tickets@blazingswan.com.au

### [Can I get a refund if the event is cancelled?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

If our event is cancelled holders of valid tickets will be refunded where this is provided for in the Ticket and Event Terms and Conditions.

### [What if I can’t find my tickets?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

Your ticket will come to you as an email, to the email address you nominated when purchasing the ticket.  The sender will be Humanitix.  Check your junk mail or spam mail folders as well as your inbox.  If you still can’t see it, follow the link below:

[Click this link to go to the how to find my ticket instructions](https://humanitix.helpdocs.io/)

### [Should I bring a printed ticket?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

All tickets will be emailed to you by Humanitix. Please print this ticket, or downloaded it as an image or file on to your phone to show the gate on arrival.

Note – Due to poor mobile phone reception at the Event site, you should make sure you save your ticket to your phone as an image or file  **before you leave home** to avoid gate hold ups.

Make sure your screen is not cracked as this can make the bar code unreadable. If your screen is cracked we recommend you print your ticket and bring that with you.  Please protect the bar code on your ticket from prying eyes.  Don’t celebrate by posting a picture of it on the internet !

### [What is the deal with wristbands?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

When you arrive at the Event Gate and present a valid Ticket you will given a wrist band which will be secured on your wrist.  This wristband must remain secured on your wrist for the duration of your attendance at the Event.  If your wristband becomes damaged contact Blazing Swan and bring the damaged wristband and proof that you hold a valid Ticket and we will arrange a replacement wristband.

Anyone found onsite without a wristband may be asked for proof that they hold a valid Ticket, and may be expelled from the Event site.  Under 18’s wearing an Adult wristband may be expelled from the event site, along with their parents or guardians and siblings

Blazing Swan takes no responsibility for what might happen if you continue to wear ALL your wristbands from your attendance at all of our previous events.  But we will be impressed.

### [Who do I contact if I have a question about or problem with tickets?](https://blazingswan.com.au/ticket-faq/#)

For all your ticket enquires, please contact the Blazing Swan ticket team at tickets(at)blazingswan.com.au   If you are on the Humanitix Event page you can use the ‘Contact Host’ button to send us a message.

Blazing Swan 2026 is fully sold out.

WE DO NOT RECOMMEND purchasing tickets from online sites or from strangers in the street!  Every year we hear reports of people being scammed.  If you are scammed you can let us, and Scamwatch, know and we will warn other people.  But you will have to contact the Police if you wish to take action against the scammer.  You might also contact your bank or credit card provider.

[Get your tickets here](https://events.humanitix.com/blazing-swan-2026-takes-a-village?_gl=1*vdr8w3*_gcl_au*NDY5Njg0NzgzLjE3NjMwMzQxNDk.*_ga*MTkwODMzMjkyNS4xNzU0NzM1MTI3*_ga_LHKW5FR9N6*czE3NjMwMzQxNDkkbzIkZzEkdDE3NjMwMzQxOTIkajE3JGwwJGgw)

## Blazing Swan Tickets and Event Attendance Terms and Conditions

Yes, we have rules.  You need to be aware of them before you purchase tickets.

Read them here – [Blazing Swan Tickets and Event Attendance Terms and Conditions](https://blazingswan.com.au/terms-conditions/)
