# Welcome to our Event FAQ’s

Burning Questions? Burning Answers

## Planning and Preparation

### [What is Blazing Swan?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**Blazing Swan is an annual event celebrating art and community and individuality in line with the [Principles of Blazing Swan and Burning Man](https://blazingswan.com.au/11-principles/).**

Blazing Swan provide grants and assistance to people to help bring visual or performance art to the Event.   Everyone at the Event is an artist, everyone is a performer, and everyone is part of this community.  Blazing Swan is an officially recognized member of the Burning Man Regional Network, drawing inspiration from the Burning Man Event in the USA.  Blazing Swan is not a doof or a rave. It’s not a cult or an exclusive community.

Blazing Swan does not stand apart from the world or ‘regular’ existence.  When you become part of Blazing Swan, Blazing Swan becomes part of you.  Friendships you make here will endure, ideas you find here and share here will grow.  Blazing Swan is more than a seven day, once a year thing.

### [When is the Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**In 2026 the Event runs from noon on Wednesday 1 April to noon on Tuesday 7 April.**

Every year the Blazing Swan event opens at noon on the Wednesday immediately prior to Easter Sunday, and closes at noon on the Tuesday immediately following Easter Sunday.  Friday to Monday is a is a public holiday  and many Australians travel to the countryside.  The roads will be very busy, the police will be very active, and hire vehicles are booked up months in advance.  The date of Easter Sunday in Australia can be anywhere from 22 March to 25  April.

### [Where is the Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**The Event is held near the town of Kulin in Western Australia**

The Event is held on farmland 15km east of Kulin beside Jilakin Lake.   When not being used by Blazing Swan the site hosts a community horse carnival (October), and for the rest of the year it is used for growing crops and pasture.  This is the Country of the Njaki Njaki people and we ask participants to respect their relationship with the land, and to respect the Kulin community who have been good friends to Blazing Swan over many years.  Kulin is not just where we hold the Event, it is our home.

### [What weather can I expect?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**It can be very challenging.  Do not undestimate the dangers of severe weather.**

The Event site is exposed and subject to high winds.  At night it can be close to freezing, and days can be up to 40°C (105°F).  There can be thunderstorms and hail, and parts of the Event site may flood.  There is also the possibility of dust storms.  The Event organisers will share weather forecasts via FM Radio and our Centre Kiosk infomation point.

### [Do you have rules?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**Yes.**  There are rules to keep you and other people as safe and comfortable as possible.  There are rules to comply with local and State regulations and laws, and there are rules to ensure that we can continue to present the Event next year, and the year after that.  Why is it that Burn Events around the world have more rules than almost any other sort of Event?  Maybe because we care more for each other.  And because multi-day events in harsh environments (yes, that’s us) require more rules to keep everyone safe.

The Rules are in the [Blazing Swan Tickets and Event Attendance Terms and Conditions](https://blazingswan.com.au/terms-conditions/).  They are signposted at the Gate.  They are written into our policies and Principles and Official Statements.  If you’re not sure, ask.

### [Who is welcome at the Blazing Swan Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**Blazing Swan is a ticketed event.**   Ticket numbers for the event are limited.   Members of the Blazing Swan Association, volunteers and members of accredited Theme Camps are given the first option of purchasing tickets to the Event.  Any remaining tickets will be offered for sale to the public.  Our tickets are sold through a not-for-profit organisation which directs the additional charges it levies towards charities.  Blazing Swan is a not-for-profit organisations which directs any surplus revenue towards running the event and supporting arts in line with its Constitution.

Special categories of tickets are available for children, for recognized carers of attendees, and for Kulin locals   With the exception of Kulin locals, all classes of tickets are for the full seven day Event.

Blazing Swan reserves the right to not sell a ticket to any person for any reason.  Any person who is in breach of the [Blazing Swan Tickets and Event Attendance  Terms and Conditions](https://blazingswan.com.au/terms-conditions/) may have their permission to remain at the Event withdrawn without compensation and with immediate effect by Blazing Swan Incorporated.

### [How can I prepare for the Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**Follow the Principle of ‘Radical Self Reliance’ and do your own research.**

*   Look for and take advice from friends who have been to Blazing Swan
*   Connect with people, stories and information through social media, our website and the internet generally.
*   Look into specific topics such as ‘bush cooking’, ‘staying healthy while camping’ and information about Kulin and Western Australia’s Wheatbelt Region.  Remember though, ground fires are forbiden in all areas, and in camping areas you can only use gas, butane or propane cookers.

**Think ahead**

*   If you are working – book your leave early.  You’ll be looking for a few extra days off around Easter.  Note that School Holidays usually start on the Friday prior to Easter Sunday.
*   Arrange to leave your pets with a friend.  No pets are allowed at the Blazing Swan Event.
*   If you are a volunteer coming to the Event site early (or staying late) find someone to mind your children.  Children are not permitted on the worksite prior to the Event opening, or after it closes.
*   Leave sufficient time to travel to and from Kulin.  Make sure you and your vehicle are in good condition.  Car repairs and parts can not be obtained at the ‘last minute’.
*   If you are hiring a vehicle or camper, get in early.   There’s lots of demand for Easter bookings.
*   Make time to be creative, to make costumes, to prepare frozen meals and to pack carefully.  Don’t leave this until the last moment.
*   Make a plan for keeping in touch with anyone you need to keep in touch with.  There is only Telstra mobile phone/data coverage at the Event.  If you have a special need, contact the Event organisers.

**Organise**

*   Organise with your friends (and make friends) to attend the Event together and to share resources at the Event
*   Come together before the Event to make plans, be creative and to prepare food and frozen meals
*   Join a Theme Camp
*   Volunteer with Blazing Swan

**Practice**

*   Test all your gear.  If your tent/trailer etc is new set it up at home (or in a local park) in daylight before coming out to Blazing Swan.
*   Start thinking about reducing the MOOP (Matter Out of Place) in your life BEFORE you come to the Event.  Reduce the amount of packaging, recycle more effectnively, repair rather than replace.

**Brace yourself and pace yourself**

*   Expect the unexpected and go with the flow
*   Relax and energise, stay chilled, and excited
*   Stay healthy, treat minor bangs and scrapes with your first aid kit before they turn into something major.
*   If you’re coming with people you are in an intimate relationship with, talk about spending time together and time apart.  Making space for each other and each other’s needs.
*   Have a personal safe space, and get to know the safe (quiet) spaces at the Event.
*   When it’s hot, drink before you’re thirsty.  Piss clear !  And don’t forget – in all the excitement – to eat.
*   Practice self care, mutual care, and radical caring for strangers.  Be open to help from others.

**Use protection**

*   Label your gear, even if travelling with friends.  When everything is covered in dust everything looks the same.
*   Leave your valuables at home
*   Use protection

You can read more in our [Survival Guide](https://blazingswan.com.au/survival-guide/)

## Coming and Going

### [What must I bring?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**Your e-ticket and photo ID. Your ticket can either be saved on your phone (no cracked screens please) or printed.**

You or the group you are with must bring your own shelter, and sufficient food and water (4 litres per person per day) for the duration of the Event.  There is nothing for sale at the Event.

### [What should I bring?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**The necessary things**

For a list of things [see the checklist](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vRCjokNRIAsNslenW_hndOa7fDFNsW_ySChE5yjhiDDOxtFbiOLltOlyEDN2TSeSafSYmBR5Ra2wy5c/pub).

Blazing Swan isn’t just about the praciticalities. Bring toys or costumes which express your creative spirit.  Keep an eye out on the Blazing Swan socual media for the annual ‘Costumery Thread’ which lists all the themed parties, marches etc and gives you a chance to get out to the Op Shops or make your own!

Consider sharing between friends, or making friends in order to share.  Use Blazing Swan’s social media to reach out to others with collaborative projects. Sharing a toothbrush might not be an option, but you could share a tube of toothpaste.  One less thing for one of you to bring.  Explore the possibilities.

**The Ideas and the expression**

Make art, make music – bring an instrument or bring a choir.  Scan the event schedule for Blazing Swan when it becomes available.  Many Theme Camps invite people to gift performances or talks.  Be a performance, dress up or dress down – be the personification of a Principle of Blazing Swan, or of all of them.  If you plan on doing, that’s great.  But also make time to do nothing.  Leave space to soak up what other people have brought to the Event.

**Get you head around the Principle of ‘Gifting’  It’s not quite what you expect**

You are not expected to bring a gift, nor is anyone expected to offer you a gift at Blazing Swan. If you DO receive a gift you are not required or expected to give one in return. You might be uncomfortable with that.  If you give a gift, you should not expect one in return.  You might be uncomfortable with that too.  That’s intentional, and it takes some getting used to.  The Principle of Gifting challenges us to see the world not in terms of debt and obligation, but in terms of connection and opportunity.  When we gift freely, the world becomes richer.  Remember also that gifts are not always things.  Sometime the most profound gift is simply making time for someone, or sharing your joy with someone.  Give it a go.

### [What should I leave at home?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**Glass** containers and bottles are not welcome at Blazing Swan.

**Drones** that are not pre-approved by Blazing Swan will not be permitted at the Event.

**Pets** are not allowed. If you bring an animal that is not an approved assistance animal to the event, you will be asked to leave..

**Lasers** that are not pre-approved by Blazing Swan will not be permitted at the Event.

For a more complete list, see the [Blazing Swan Tickets and Event Attendance Terms and Conditions](https://blazingswan.com.au/terms-conditions/).

### [Can I bring my registered assistance animal?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**Assistance Animals.**  Participants at the Blazing Swan event who require the assistance of a Assistance Animal and whose Assistance Animal meets Australian Federal Law regarding Assistance Animals as laid out in the Disability Discrimination Act, may be accompanied by their Assistance Animal where required.

Please inform Accessibility Lead as soon as possible.

Your Assistance Animal will require a species specific Veterinary certification of health to be emailed to Accessibility Lead at [accessibility@blazingswan.com.au](mailto:accessibility@blazingswan.com.au) that also shows any and all blood tests appropriate have been done, faecal floats, including addressing zoonotics if any, and all worming and vaccinations required have been administered.

This IS a higher standard than the average entry to a supermarket Public Access Test.  Firstly because this event takes place on farmland and it is not acceptable to bring anything untoward onto farmland.  Secondly, there are areas of Blaze where people are packed together tightly, and we don’t want any diseases or parasites being passed onto or spread among humans. Please contact Accessibility Lead for suggestions of Assistance Animal specialty vets in WA to aquire your pre Blaze certificate, if you require help.

In the case  of working canines: Identification and proof that the dog is an Approved Assistance Dog Cardholder, or under which DDA clause it is working, and dossier if clause (C), is required.

For Non Canine Assistance Animals, both Medical BioMonitors and PsycoSocial Support, please email under what clause of the DDA your Assistance Animal is working, and provide the standard dossier of proof.  For those not accustomed to going out in public with their NCAA, please email Accessibility Lead for assistance. Please include your NCAA’s task list, training level, how they help you, and a bit about you and them.

If you are unsure if your animal is an Assistance Animal yet it alleviates your disability and is exceptionally highly trained, please contact Acessibility Lead for a conversation and assessment asap.

Because pets are not permitted, if you require your Assistance Animal with you in order to attend Blazing Swan, we require that you pre-register your Assistance Animal by sending an email to  Accessibility Lead [accessibility@blazingswan.com.au](mailto:accessibility@blazingswan.com.au)

We warn all participants that the “Event” venue often presents unforgiving physical environments for humans and animals alike. Inclement weather, fire, loud noises, crowds and flashing lights are all common, and if any of these would be too uncomfortable or pose a risk for either you or your Assistance Animal we ask that you carefully consider these factors as you decide whether to participate, with or without your Assistance Animal.

If you bring an Assistance Animal to the “Event”, you are required to ensure:

*   the animal does not pose a risk or threat to any other person or Assistance Animals at the “Event”
*   the health and safety of that animal at all times;
*   the animal is in your control, or the control of a person known to you, at all times, which generally requires that the animal be on a leash or harness, or in an appropriate enclosure.

If you have any questions please email –  [accessibility@blazingswan.com.au](mailto:accessibility@blazingswan.com.au)

### [What are my transport options to and from Kulin?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**The Event site is 290km (180 miles) inland from Perth, just beyond the town of Kulin.  Your can get there by car, bus or rideshare.**

If you are driving give your vehicle a check-over before you set out, don’t overload it and take your time.  Avoid travelling to Kulin at sunrise, or returning to Perth at sunset – the sun will be be direcly in your eyes.  There will be a massive police presence on the roads simply because it is the Easter holidays.  Both the police and hundreds of locals will – somehow – instantly identify you as Blazers and word gets back to us.  Don’t speed through local towns, it trashes our reputation.  If you see a kangaroo cross the road, slow down.  There’s almost always another one coming just behind.  At high speed, drive straight and brake – you’ll survive a head on with a roo.  But swerve and you’ll die.  Mobile phone coverage drops out at points along the way, so work out where you’re going before your set out.  Don’t drive tired – that’s the major killer on country roads.  If you need to, pull completely off the road into a parking bay – you are sharing some very narrow roads with some very heavy trucks.

The [Transwa Bus service from Perth to Kulin](https://www.transwa.wa.gov.au/tickets-times/coach-timetables) runs on Thursdays and Sundays, with a return ride on Tuesdays.   The bus stop is in Kulin, but if you hang around the hotel or the shop there’ll be someone coming along who will give you a lift out to the Event site.  Transwa buses also visit Narrogin and Williams daily.

If you don’t have a vehicle, or if you’re looking to minimise your carbon footprint, rideshare might be the thing for you.  Blazing Swan set up a facebook group each year which you can join.  If you need a ride, or have space to share a ride, connect up there.   If you’ve got up to Blazing Swan but don’t have a ride (yet) back to Perth, register at Centre Kiosk.

### [Can I pick up supplies on my way to the Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Self-reliance is a big thing at Blazing Swan. Everything you need, you need to bring with you.

That said, you can do some of your shopping in Kulin, just 17kmfrom the Event site.  The [IGA supermarket in Kulin](https://www.iga.com.au/stores/iga-kulin/) has limited stocks, but you CAN pre-order and pre-pay and pick up your supplies there.  You’ll need to put in your order at least a week ahead.  The [Kulin Community Hub](https://www.facebook.com/KulinCommunityHub6365/) (community owned pub) has limited take away, but again you can pre-order and pre-pay.  The [Kulin Mitre 10 hardware store](https://www.facebook.com/kulin.hardware.rural/) has a good range of supplies.

Be aware that these Kulin outlets have limited hours – especially around Easter.  Check the links above.  Note also that the [nearest Chemist is in Corrigin](https://corriginpharmacy.com.au/), 55km from Kulin.  Finally, please note that Blazing Swan discourages people from leaving and returning to Event site to pick up extra supplies, so get all your gear on your way in.

A [24 hour self-service fuel station](https://www.kulin.wa.gov.au/live/facilities/24-hour-fuel-facility.aspx) is available at Kulin (standard unleaded and diesel).   LPG Autogas is available at [Gasworks Narrogin](http://narrogingasworx.com.au/) (limited hours) and Ampol Williams (24 hours) .  There are [two EV chargers at Kulin](https://www.plugshare.com/location/128254) operated by the Shire, one Tesla 22 kw and one 32A 3-phase non-networked.

### [When are the Event gates open?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Remember that the Gate opens to the public at noon on the WEDNESDAY prior to the Easter weekend.  Aim to get to the Event site during daylight hours.  Give yourself plenty of time to get from wherever you’re coming from.  Drive carefully and take breaks.

### [Can I drive on site?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

You may drive directly to your camping spot, but do not plan to use your vehicle as transportation on site for the duration of your stay. This is a serious safety issue and will be strictly enforced

*   For safety – arriving after sunset will result in you being asked to park in a temporary holding area. You can then walk to your camping spot to set up
*   No driving will be allowed on site during the Event without a Blazing Swan DMT (Department of Mutant Transport) permit
*   Site speed limit is 8 km/hr on all roads, to avoid any vehicle/pedestrian interactions and keep the dust down
*   If you are camping with a Theme Camp you will be directed to those (otherwise) closed areas.
*   Pedestrians and cyclists always have right of way on all access roads

### [When can we leave the Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Well yes, you can eventually. It’s not Hotel California.  But we discourage people from ‘popping out’ and returning during the Event, as it creates extra traffic movements –  and vehicles moving around the event are a risk to pedestrians.   We normally levy a $20 fee for vehicles leaving and returning to the event site.

However, people may have good reasons to leave and come back, to pick up something from the pharmacy in Corrigin, or even to attend to an emergency in Perth.  In ALL cases we ask that you check in with the site management BEFORE heading out.  If you expect to have to ‘come and go’ we recommend you leave your vehicle parked near the gate.

### [When must we leave Blazing Swan?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

If you aren’t volunteering with Blazing Swan, or a member of a Theme Camp you MUST leave the site by noon on the Tuesday following Easter.  Have a designated driver and make sure that person has a quiet Monday night and gets a good sleep.  And/or let them sleep longer on Tuesday morning while everyone else packs up.   Pack your vehicle carefully (including all your MOOP) and do all the usual checks.  Make sure your camping site is left spotless.  Leave No Trace !  Drive carefully.  Pick up fuel and some refreshments in Kulin.  Do NOT dump your rubbish in Kulin, take it home with you.  Take it easy on the way back to wherever you came from or wherever you are going.

### [While I'm here, what else can I see and do?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Blazing Swan committee and crew work hard to build a strong relationship with local residents, service providers and the Shire of Kulin. With thousands of participants passing through Kulin, we have a significant impact on this normally quiet country town.   Drive slowly, be polite. patient, and respectful. We are guests here.

There’s more to Kulin than just Blazing Swan.  The water slide (hard not to see) is usually closed by the time Blaze come around each year, but [check out the other local attractions](https://www.wheatbelttourism.com/where-to-stay/kulin/).   If you’re in travelling mode you can head East from here to Wave Rock, or south to the Stirling Ranges and the South Coast, or down through the South West to Margaret River   This year – as in most years – [the Folkword/Fairbridge 3 day music festival](https://fairbridgefestival.com.au/) follows hot on the heels of Blaze.  It’s a great place to decompress.  Your wardrobe will blend in (they do require clothes),  but you’ll recognize your fellow Blazers because they’ll be dustier than the rest.

### [Can I come early, or stay after the Event, or visit the event site at other times of the year?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

No.  Unless you are pre-approved by Blazing Swan to assist with the setup or the packdown (we are always looking for volunteers for this) of the site you must not arrive prior to noon on Wednesday 1 April 2026 and you must leave by noon on Tuesday 7 April 2026.

The event site is private property and is NOT open for camping or even to visit at other times of the year.  HOWEVER, there is free camping and a caravan park in Kulin, and you can come out and visit JILAKIN ROCK – the entrance is on the other side of the road from the event site.  You are NOT permitted to camp there overnight.

## At The Event

### [What can I do at the Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Blazing Swan will be very clear about what you must not do – what the Rules are, and what is not allowed.  Read all about it in the Terms and Conditions on your Ticket.

But what about the things we recommend you do at Blazing Swan?  Everyone’s ‘best’ Blazing Swan experience is different, but here’s some tips we’ve picked up over the years…

*   Eat well and stay hydrated!
*   Watch the sunrise and sunset from Cave Rock
*   Be there for the Welcome to Country
*   Watch the Effigy Burn on Saturday night and join in afterwards
*   Watch the Temple procession and Burn on Sunday night
*   Line up for some morning coffee at ‘Black Lagoon’ and pancakes at ‘Steampunk Pancakes’
*   Be there for the Big Dress Parade
*   Dress up for the themed events
*   Check out the artwork and the artcars
*   Sample all the musical offerings
*   Chill out in the chill out spaces
*   Join the nude shoot
*   Most of the volunteer positions will already be taken, but check in at Centre Kiosk to see if more are required, or to sign up for next year!
*   Meet your neighbours
*   Help a stranger and accept help from a stranger.
*   When you see something or experience something great, recommend it to a friend

Read the WTF (Where’s the Fun) Guide and follow the map to all the sites and all the things.   If you’ve lost your copy (it’s a good idea to keep one copy in your camp) pop up to Centre Kiosk to see the big notice boards and maybe pick up a spare copy of the WTF.  Check the Dust App on your phone (hint, after loading switch you phone to Aeroplane mode)

### [Can I buy and sell things at the Event](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**No, you may not sell or buy things at our Event.**

We practice the principle of DECOMMODIFICATION at our Event.  It is an opportunity to imagine a world based on friendship and generous spirit and actions.  We do not trade, or even exchange.  We simply GIVE without expectation of reward or acknowledgement, and we respectfully accept the GIFTS given us.

It’s not easy to do this when you are surrounded by the pressure of advertising and commerce, and the real struggle to provide for ourselves and those we love.  That’s why we are so particular about not bringing advertising or commerce to Blazing Swan.  Blazing Swan is absolutely part of the World.  If it wasn’t, we couldn’t say that there’s some hope that what we do here might change the World, even just a little for the better.  But let’s practice our perfect World in our perfect World here at Blazing Swan.  Then when we go home and when we catch ourselves listening to the siren call of commerce, we know we can dial it down a bit, because we’ve practiced doing without it already, and because we know there’s something more important.

### [Where can I fill up my Water Bottle?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

**You need to bring all the water you will need for the week with you**.

We recommend at least 4 litres per day – this water will cover you for drinking, cooking and washing. Radical Self Reliance!

### [Can I get ice at the Event?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

This is where Decommodification and Radical Self Reliance meets Communal Effort and Civic Responsibility.   We don’t want your food to go off and we certainly don’t want people coming down with food poisoning.  So we provide bags of ice at a standard country town price.   

*   Ice must be pre-ordered online.  Orders open in early March.  There are no cash sales on site
*   Ice comes in 5kg bags.  Order as many as you need.  Pick up your order on any/every day of the event
*   Times and location for pick-ups will be announced closer to the event.  Or check in with Centre Kiosk who know ‘everything’.
*   Bring a trolley or a friend if you’re picking up more than one bag of ice

### [Are there showers?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Sure.  Cold showers. Remember that water is incredibly precious at Blaze.  Here’s one wrong way and three right ways to do it:

*   You could have a shower.  If you keep it down to four minutes, we’re looking at (best) around 60 litres.  Aaaarghhh!
*   You could use the (1) shower (2) lather (3) shower-rinse method.  Turning the shower off while you do the lather phase.   You might get this down to 10 litres
*   You could use the (1) bucket+cup (2) lather (3) bucket+cup method.  You can easily get this down to 5 litres.  Carry the water bucket with a sturdy handle (it can be warm water!) to the shower block and wash there.  Use the cup to pour water over your head and body.
*   You could use the (1) mist-spray (2) lather (3) bucket+cup method.  You can get this down to 2 to 3 litres.  Again, do this at the shower block, not on the ground beside your tent

You can cut down further by using baby/wet wipes in-between times.  Use the eco friendly types if you can find them, and take the used ones home with you for disposal.

### [Are there toilets?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Yes there are toilets  – lots of them, so use them.  Pissing and pooping all over the countryside is not on.  So don’t do it.

Toilets are being constantly cleaned, adopt one yourself and be a toilet-hero.  You can decorate a toilet BUT please don’t put adhesive stickers on them.  We have to pay a huge penalty to the toilet hire people.   With portaloos leave the seat down when you’re finished – that way the ventilation works properly.  We supply double ply paper because the portaloo people tell us it’s ok, but don’t bring your 9-ply magic soft paper, or put things down the loo that didn’t come straight out of your body.

Experiment with female urination devices.  Practice in the shower at home!  If it’s a long way to the toilets, use a pee bottle at night – and empty it in the toilets next day.  Oh, and careful which bottle you reach for first thing in the morning to slake your thirst.  Been there done that…

If you find a toilet that’s not working, give the Event organisers a shout.  That way it’ll get fixed and everyone is happy.

### [When do we burn things?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

There are two main burns during Blazing Swan. Typically the Saturday night is the Effigy Burn, and the Sunday night is the Temple Burn.   The Effigy Burn is the loud party one, the Temple Burn is the quiet respectful one.  Obey all instructions of officials at the Burns.  Non-consensual photography is obsolutely forbidden during the usual post-Effigy Burn celebration (and anytime!).  Don’t let anyone spoil anybody’s special moments at Blazing Swan.

Both Burns are dependent on suitable weather for safety.   We’ll look at the situation and let people know.  If you’re planing on visiting the Temple please be aware that it will be closed off to the public from the morning of the scheduled Burn onwards.  So get there on the days prior.

It’s very possible that other artworks will be burnt during the week.  Check in with Centre Kiosk to see what’s scheduled.

### [Are we on a Playa? Really?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

The ground you are standing on is not a Playa.  A ‘playa’ is a dried salt lake.  Lake Jilakin is a playa, although there’s usually a bit of water in it at this time of year.  You’re standing on a paddock, or field, that’s actually used to grow crops (barley, lupin, etc) and run sheep when we’re not around.  The locals know it as the Kulin Bush Race Track.  A while back – 70 million years or so –  it was the valley of the Pingrup River, flowing south down to the Great Rift Valley between Australian and Antarctica.  Dinosaur country.

### [What do I do if I have a problem?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

The Medical Centre and Rangers HQ are in/around Camp Hart – the building just to the North of the Racetrack.  Patrolling Rangers (wearing distinctive shirts and hats), Centre Kiosk and every Theme Camp will have a radio and can call for assistance for you.   

### [What happens with lost property?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

There is no truly Lost Property at Blazing Swan because everyone labels all their gear before they arrive.  Don’t you?

Things do get misplaced, however.  If you find something that looks like it has come adrift from its owner, you can take it to Centre Kiosk who will be handling lost property.  Likewise, if you’ve misplaced something, come and check out the gear that’s been brought to Centre Kiosk.  If it’s a valuable item bring photo ID with you.

Each year we collect enough phones to start a phone shop.  Do yourself a favour and put some contact details / your name on your screen saver, or pop a note in your phone case.

Items not claimed during the event will be advertised to our community through social media following the event.

## Camping

### [Camp I camp with my friends?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Campsites cannot be booked or reserved. If you want to camp with your friends, please plan to arrive together

### [Can I bring a gazebo?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Um, sure, yes. Just be aware that when the wind starts blowing 50-60km per hour your gazebo can easily fly away before landing on a bunch of innocent bystanders, breaking bones and puncturing soft bodies.  So if you bring a gazebo, do these things as well:  

*   Try and get a good-ish quality one. 
*   Tie it down with double guy ropes and 250-350mm ground pegs on each corner
*   Lock it down by driving star pickets at least 600mm into the ground alongside each leg, and secure the legs to the pickets
*   Chuck a rope OVER the top of the gazebo and tie that rope down either to very strong ground pegs or the star pickets
*   If you have a vehicle with good tie-down points (a roo bar or roofrack) consider lashing the gazebo to the vehicle as well.  
    

Don’t even think about beach umbrellas.  A giant stabby thing cartwheeling across the event site?  No thanks.

### [Can I bring a caravan/camper/RV/camper-trailer?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Yes.  But note that Blazing Swan does not provide electric plug-in points in the general camping area.  If you’re a member of a Theme Camp in the Theme Camp area it’s up to your Theme Camp to agree to attach you to their power.  This power IS limited, and it’s provided by Blazing Swan primarily so that Theme Camps can present (and prepare) their public offerings.  Rules about grey and black water apply to RV’s etc – truck it out with you at the end of the event and dispose responsibly.

### [Can I reserve a campsite?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

No. Come early if you need space to add friends.

### [Can I have a generator?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Sure.  It should be the muffled or silent type and operated in accordance with its instructions.  Be considerate of your neighbours and don’t run it late at night.  Be VERY careful where you store the fuel (containers should not be on the ground), and likewise be EXTREMELY careful where the exhaust goes.  A camper at a Burn event died recently from the fumes entering his tent from his neighbour’s generator.  If you just need to charge your phone pop up to Centre Kiosk, or find a friendly Theme Camp that might lend you a powerpoint for a while.  It’s your responsibility to ‘watch’ your phone in those circumstances.

### [Can I use amplified music in the camping areas?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Music is a favoured method of participation and self-expression at Blazing Swan.  That said, leave the big amplified systems to the Theme Camps operating in our special ‘Sound Camp Alley’ zone up between Cave Rock and the Lake.

Small music systems are ok in the camping areas, but be considerate of your neighbours – If someone asks you to turn your system down, you should probably turn it down, and if it’s after midnight or before 8am, maybe just turn it off entirely and go enjoy the DJs in Sound Alley

Bring your acoustic instruments – there’s always opportunities up at the Theme Camps to borrow a stage, and making music in a circle of friends in the camping area makes for a magical experience and memories.

### [Can I have a fire at my camp?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

No.  You will see some fire barrels in Theme Camps, but they will have applied for permission.  So if you are not a Theme Camp, the answer is no.

### [Can I bring my BBQ or gas cooker?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Yes, you may have a gas BBQ or gas cooker at your camp in both general camping and theme camp areas. The use of these appliances must be in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions and the Gas Cookers and Barbeques section of the Blazing Swan Fire Management Manual.

However, if the Fire Crew or Blaze Officials announce a total fire ban, then these items may not be used.  Listen carefully to instructions.

### [Can I have a fire of heater in my structure?](https://blazingswan.com.au/faq/#)

Don’t.  Just don’t do it.  Burns are horrible – burns caused by melting tent plastic dripping on you are worse than horrible.  So don’t.

If you want to keep warm in your shelter at night, borrow a trick from the (fool)hardy folk who climb Everest.  Pour hot water – carefullly – into a strong steel drink flask, seal tightly and pop the drink flask in a thick sock or two, and stuff that under your doona or into your sleeping bag.

If you are desperately cold seek assistance.  If you see someone unconscious laying on the ground outside at night, call for assistance.  Clear sky nights at Kulin can plunge down close to freezing.   Without proper shelter that can kill someone very easily and very quietly.

# **Theme Camps Information**

# **Theme Camp Applications for Blazing Swan 2027 will close on 20th December 2026**

[Apply to bring a Theme Camp to Blazing Swan 2027](https://www.cognitoforms.com/BlazingSwanIncorporated/_2027ThemeCampsApplicationForm)

### **Tell me… What is a Theme Camp?**

When a group of participants comes together in the spirit of communal effort to create and gift interactive experiences to other participants at a burn, that’s a theme camp.

Theme camps might bring music and performance, food or beverage, crafts or workshops, meditative spaces or education – there’s no one thing that theme camps are about. 

Information about some past theme camps [is here](https://blazingswan.com.au/theme-camp-history/theme-camps/).

### **Tell me… How do I bring a Theme Camp to the Blazing Swan Event?**

Creating a theme camp can take some time and commitment, and even some hard work, but it can be very rewarding as well.

All theme camps are required to operate safely, in compliance with local and state laws, and in accordance with the [11 principles](https://blazingswan.com.au/11-principles/).  

Registering your theme camp gets you access to an official spot on the map & in the ‘Where’s the Fun’ guide, and also grants you access to support and advice from Blazing Swan Inc (‘the org’) and from a network of other camps. 

Support provided by the org includes advice and guidance on operating safely, and might include things like early access to site for builds, or reserved tickets depending on need.

If you’ve been registered for 2026 be sure to join the [Theme Camp Leads group](https://www.facebook.com/share/g/1AidQMij4W/) on Facebook if you are registered as a Theme Camp. Remember, no camp is 100% good to go until they’re out on the dust and given final approval by our Safety Team.  Applying is just first step in the process, but there’s a team and the community here to help you see it through.

### **Tell me… How do I join a Theme Camp?**

Thinking of dipping your toes in burning waters and want to do it from the safety of a camp? Had a great time at a specific camp and want to gift some time or resources to helping the camp out? 

Joining a camp can be a great way to participate, gift your time and skills, and learn more about our community and our principles, but it’s not the only way – volunteering for a crew is also rewarding, and it’s not a requirement to join a camp to participate in a burn. 

Theme camps are groups of participants who’ve come together to gift an experience to the burn. While registered theme camps work with Blazing Swan Inc (the org) to make sure they operate safely and show up on the map, theme camps are separate from the org, and each camp has its own criteria and process for bringing in new helpers or new members. 

If you’re keen to join a camp, participating in the community outside of the burn (through social media and other burner events through the year) is the best way to get to know about any theme camp or volunteer opportunities that become available.

### **Tell me…. More  
**

Everyone involved in your Theme Camp should read both the regular [Blazing Swan Survival Guide](https://blazingswan.com.au/survival-guide/) and the [Theme Camps Survival Guide](https://blazingswan.com.au/wp-content/uploads/Blazing-Swan-Event-Theme-Camps-Survival-Guide.pdf).

More information and links to resources will be provided to Theme Camps when they register.

# Art Grants Information

### **Round One Art Grant Applications for 2027 are open from 1st – 27th September 2026**

### **Round Two Art Grant Applications for 2027 are open from 1st – 31st October 2026**

### **If you are inspired and want to bring your creative energy to Blazing Swan we suggest:**

READ the Art Installation Guidelines below very carefully. Come to the event and catch up with the Artists and the Blazing Swan Arts Crew and learn from their experience.  Be inspired!  You can contact our Arts Department [emailing us](mailto:artsadmin@blazingswan.com.au) – Addressing your email with “Attention ARTS’.

If you want to incorporate fire into your art, read the FIRE guidelines. All artworks involving fire must be pre-approved by our Fire Team, who can be contacted using the [Contact Form on this Website](https://blazingswan.com.au/contact-us/) – select for attention ‘FIRE’.

If you need help with you art piece or art ideas, start a discussion with people through our social media sites.

If you need to raise additonal funds for your art, consider using fundraising activities or seeking support from a fundraising site.

### When’s the best time to start planning your Blazing Swan Artwork ? Now!

### **Art installations and grants FAQ**

### [Who owns my art?](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

You do.  The art you create remains 100% yours.  That said, if you do not arrange to remove it from the event site within 2 weeks of the event concluding, we wil assume you have abandoned it and arrange to dispose of it and bill you for any expense involved in that.

### [Who can apply for Art Grants?](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

Anyone aged 18 or over, from novice to professional.

### [How are the successful Art Grant applicants selected?](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

The art will be selected by a panel who will be looking for projects that embody Blazing Swan’s 11 principles, support the theme of the event and add value to the community experience. Sending additional documentation in pdf/jpg format is highly recommended.

### [What happens if I miss getting my application in on time, or don’t get a grant?](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

Applications submitted after the round two closing date will be considered for placement only. If you do not receive a grant and decide to fund it yourself you can still register your art and have it placed in the Where’s the Fun Guide (as long as it meets safety requirements)

### [What if I make art without grant money and want to bring it along anyway?](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

If you want us to place your artwork in a public space and refer to it in our Where’s the Fun Guide and map you will still need to register it with us. Please fill out the art application form to receive support.

### [Where does all the grant money come from?](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

Grant money comes from our ticket sales.

### [Can i donate money/workshop space/equipment to the arts?](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

Even a little goes a long way so please do!

### [I have more questions!](https://blazingswan.com.au/art-grants-information-and-application/#)

*   Read more information below.
*   Read through the application form.
*   Contact ARTS using the [Contact Form](https://blazingswan.com.au/contact-us/) on this website.

### **Art Installation Guidelines**

**1\. The Challenge**

*   Creating art for Jilakin Rock City presents many challenges. You must consider the physical landscape within the Wheatbelt, the logistics of transporting props, building materials and equipment to site, as well as the challenge of using tools and equipment in a place which has no mains power and only a small market for resources (within the Town of Kulin).

**2\. Responsibility**

*   All aspects of the art piece should be carefully thought out by the artist(s) and artist(s) must be prepared to seriously consider the responsibilities that go hand in hand with creating art for an event this large.
*   Artwork must be sufficiently secured against high winds and intense weather conditions. Anchoring to the ground + Guy wires necessary for the securing of art pieces, are required to be flagged.
*   Artwork must be well illuminated at night. To prevent pedestrians or art vehicles from crashing into art pieces, all aspects of the art piece should be well-lit, including rebar and guy wires.
*   To prevent irreparable environmental damage, no holes larger than 300cm by 300cm in either direction may be dug on site. If you do need to dig a hole up to this size, you will need to keep the dirt, so you can pack it back into the hole when dismantling your installation.
*   Camping is not allowed at any art installation on site.

**3\. Early Entry.**

*   Artists can apply for early entry to the site for the purposes of installation. If you or your crew need early entry to the Blazing Swan site to set up and install your art piece, please outline this in your Art Application.
*   Anyone who needs early entry to site will require an Early Entry pass (free) in addition to their Blazing Swan ticket.
*   You must be fully self-sufficient throughout your build.

**4\. The Process**

*   When you apply for an art grant you will receive a confirmation email confirming your application.
*   Within 1-2 weeks of applications closing you will receive either a request for more information or an approval e-mail.
*   Artist Liaison is your person to chat through any issues, support you and will let you know all the things you need to do such as: signing your artist agreements, tickets + early entry, power requirements, placement details, on site support and exit survey.

**5\. Sound**

Large-scale sound art is confined to the edges of the site. Art installations that contain loud sound elements will need to be placed on the village’s outer perimeter. Some installations require a quiet area, and amplified music makes that impossible. With the open nature of the site, sound carries far and wide very easily. See our sound page for further information.

**6\. Budget + Grants**

*   The Art team is not responsible for fully funding any art project. Artists are strongly encouraged to find alternate funding for their art and to use grants as a way to supplement their work.
*   Art grants are on offer as a contribution to the costs of building and transporting your art piece to Blazing Swan. If you would like to apply for a grant you must complete the grant application form prior to the closing dates. Grant applications will be considered by a selection panel of artists and community members against the following criteria.
    *   Viability
    *   Integrity
    *   Impact
    *   Interactivity
    *   Engagement + Accessibility
    *   Relevance to Principles or Theme
    *   Environmental Responsibility
    *   [Further detail on the criteria can be found here](https://blazingswan.com.au/wp-content/uploads/Art-Grant-Selection-Criteria.pdf)
*   You must complete and submit an itemised budget with your grant application to be considered by the selection panel. If you are successful, 70% of your grant will be paid prior to the event. **The remaining 30% will be paid post- event and is dependent on delivery of outcome, deinstallation and strike. You must also submit accompanying receipts as they relate to your budget within 2 weeks for the remainder of the grant to be paid out.**
*   An art grant does not cover; Your time, warehouse hire, generic tool purchase, previous pieces that have already been funded (however you may apply for a grant to refresh it or for transport costs)
*   If you do not receive an art grant your art can still be registered and placed should you still wish to bring it.

**7\. Leave No Trace**

Leave No Trace is one of the core principles of Blazing Swan and art is no exception. A blank canvas is provided for participants at the beginning of the event on which to create a unique mark, and at the end of the event a blank canvas is all that should be left behind. All traces of Art pieces that burn, MUST BE REMOVED.

**8\. Fire and Flame Effects**

We love burning things but there are special requirements if your artwork incorporates FIRE in any way. [Read more about Art Installation Fire Guidelines.](https://blazingswan.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2019-08-31_Art-Installation-Fires-Guidelines_GDL-001-1.0.pdf)

*   Open Fire: Flames created by candles, torches, fire barrels, wood fires, and/or artwork that will itself be engulfed in flame or otherwise burned.
*   Flame Effects: Flames that are automated, switched, pressurised or have any action other than simply being lit on fire. This includes projects that use gas or liquid fuels.
*    Pyrotechnic Display: Explosives, fireworks or projectiles.
*   Hazardous Materials Storage: Storage of hazardous or combustible materials, including kerosene, gas, petrol, pyrotechnics, etc.If your artwork incorporates fire in any of those ways, it is mandatory that you contact the Fire Safety coordinator as soon as possible to discuss your plans: fire@blazingswan.com.au Failure to do so will leave us no choice but to remove this component from your installation.

[Click here to apply](https://www.cognitoforms.com/BlazingSwanIncorporated/_2027BlazingSwanArtApplications)

Once you collect three stamps, you can enter a lottery at the information desk and have a chance to win a discount coupon that can be used at Brand Avenue. There is no minimum purchase amount required to receive a stamp. You can only receive one stamp at a single booth, regardless of how many times you shop there. Please note that the stamp is awarded based on the number of purchases, not the number of items purchased. As for discount coupons, you could win a 5,000 yen discount coupon if you spend a large amount. Please visit lots of booths, do some shopping, and enter the raffle! #### FAQ

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Are there any purchase limits for certain products?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

For products with purchase limits at the atmos Merchandise Booth, the maximum number of items that can be purchased per person will be listed in the web catalog available at the venue on the event day. Purchase limits vary by product, so please check the web catalog at the venue. Please note that purchase limits and purchasing procedures may differ depending on the exhibitor at each booth. For details, please check directly at each booth.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Will there be lottery sales at the venue on the event day?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

For products available through lottery sales on the event day, details will be announced on the official atmoscon Instagram account as they become available.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Will products be sold until they are out of stock?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Products available at the venue are limited in quantity. Except for some items, products will be sold on a first-come, first-served basis until they are sold out.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I try on the products before purchasing?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Trying on products is not available at the atmos Merchandise Booth.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Is it possible that the sales methods or rules may change on the event day?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Depending on the situation at the venue, the sales methods and rules may be changed at the discretion of our staff when necessary.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I receive a refund, return, or exchange after purchasing a product?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

All sales are final. We cannot accept refunds, returns, or exchanges for products after purchase.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Do I need a ticket to purchase products at the venue?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

A valid admission ticket for the event day is required to purchase products at the venue.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Where can I purchase tickets?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Tickets are available through Lawson Ticket. For atmos member presale tickets (Exclusive Offer / Members Only), please refer to the information provided to eligible members. Same-day tickets will be available at the venue reception.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Why do ticket prices vary depending on the sales period?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Tickets are offered at lower prices during earlier sales periods. Each sales period is available only while supplies last and may end once the allocated number of tickets has been sold. We recommend purchasing your tickets early to receive the best available price.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I cancel my ticket or change the event date after purchase?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

No. Cancellations, changes, and refunds requested for personal reasons are not permitted. Except in the event of a cancellation, tickets are non-refundable once purchased.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I transfer or resell my ticket?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Ticket resale for commercial purposes is prohibited by law. Please note that tickets purchased through unauthorized resale channels will not be accepted for admission.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Will same-day tickets be available?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Same-day tickets for 1-day admission and live stage admission are scheduled to be available for purchase at the venue reception each day, while supplies last. Same-day sales will not be available for 1-Day Admission with Early Entry or 2-Day Admission. Please note that if any ticket type sells out in advance, same-day tickets for that ticket type will not be available.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

In what order will guests be admitted to the Live Stage?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

For each session, guests who have a “Live Stage Admission + 1-Day Admission” ticket will be admitted first, in the order of the queue numbers assigned to their tickets. After that, guests who have a “Live Stage Add-on” ticket will be admitted in the order they arrive at the designated meeting point. Please note that the queue number for “1-Day Admission with Early Entry” is only for early entry to the 1F Main Area and does not affect the order of admission to the Live Stage.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Why don’t Live Stage Add-on tickets have a queue number?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

The “Live Stage Add-on” ticket is for guests who already have an admission ticket for the same day and wish to add access to the Live Stage. No queue number is assigned to Live Stage Add-on tickets. If you wish to enter the Live Stage in queue-number order, please purchase a “Live Stage Admission + 1-Day Admission” ticket.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

What is the difference between "1-Day Admission with Early Entry" and "1-Day Admission"?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

A 1-Day Admission with Early Entry ticket allows you to enter the 1F Main Area before general admission. Entry is in numerical order based on your assigned entry number. A 1-Day Admission ticket allows entry starting from the general admission time.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

What is the difference between "Live Stage Admission" and "Live Stage Add-on"?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Live Stage Admission is a ticket package that includes both admission to the venue on the applicable day and access to the Live Stage. Live Stage Add-on is an additional ticket for guests who already have a valid admission ticket for the applicable day and would like to add Live Stage access. It cannot be used as a standalone ticket for venue entry.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I enter the venue with only a Live Stage Add-on ticket?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

No. A valid admission ticket for the applicable day (1-Day Admission, 1-Day Admission with Early Entry, or 2-Day Admission) is required in addition to the Live Stage Add-on ticket.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I access the Live Stage with a 2-Day Admission ticket?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

No. A 2-Day Admission ticket only includes access to the 1F Main Area on both event days. To watch the Live Stage, you will need to purchase an additional Daytime Live Stage Add-on or Night Live Stage Add-on ticket for the performance you wish to attend.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

If I want to watch both the daytime and night Live Stage performances on November 1, what tickets do I need?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

You will need both a Daytime Live Stage Admission ticket and a Night Live Stage Admission ticket (or both a Daytime Live Stage Add-on ticket and a Night Live Stage Add-on ticket). (Live Stage Add-on tickets are only for guests who already have a valid admission ticket for the applicable day and cannot be used as standalone tickets for venue entry.)

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

What is the entry number used for?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

The entry number determines the order of Early Entry to the 1F Main Area and the admission order for the Live Stage. For Live Stage tickets, the entry number indicates the order of admission to the Live Stage only and does not apply to the admission order for the 1F Main Area.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

How do I enter the venue?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Please present your ticket screen at the reception. After verification, you will receive a wristband. We kindly ask that you present the original ticket screen from your purchase rather than a screenshot.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

What happens if I arrive late for my assigned entry number time?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Your assigned entry number will become invalid, and you will be admitted from the end of the line. Please arrive with sufficient time.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I re-enter the venue after leaving?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Yes. Re-entry is permitted on the same day only. When re-entering, please make sure to wear the wristband provided at your initial entry and present it at the venue entrance.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Will there be ID checks?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

You may be asked to present a valid ID upon entry, when purchasing products, participating in lotteries, or purchasing alcoholic beverages. Please bring a valid photo ID, such as a driver’s license, Basic Resident Registration Card, passport, student ID with photo, residence card, My Number Card, or disability certificate.  
  
Please note that expired IDs, copies, or photos of IDs shown on a smartphone will not be accepted. IDs not listed above (such as employee ID cards) will not be accepted, even if multiple forms are presented.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

I have lost or damaged my wristband. Can it be reissued?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Wristbands cannot be reissued for any reason. If you are not wearing your wristband, you will not be permitted to enter the venue, even if you can provide your ticket purchase history. After putting on your wristband, please be careful not to cut it, remove it, or detach it.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

What should I do with my wristband for a 2-Day Admission ticket on the second day?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

The wristband for a 2-Day Admission ticket is valid for both event days. Please continue wearing the wristband you received on the first day and do not remove or cut it before returning on the second day. If you remove or lose your wristband after the first day, you will not be permitted to enter on the second day. Reissuance or refunds will not be provided. If you wish to enter the venue, you will need to purchase a same-day ticket again.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Is there a cloakroom or luggage storage service available?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

No cloakroom or luggage storage service is available. Please take care of your personal belongings at all times.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can minors attend the event?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Yes, minors are welcome to attend. However, children of junior high school age or younger must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.  
  
Alcoholic Beverages:  
Alcoholic beverages will be available at the venue. However, in accordance with Japanese law, we cannot sell or serve alcohol to anyone under the age of 20. Age verification may be required when purchasing alcoholic beverages.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Is admission free for children?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Admission to the 1F Main Area is free for guests who are high school age or younger. If it is difficult to confirm your age, you may be asked to provide proof of age at the reception, such as a student ID. If your age cannot be verified, paid admission will be required.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I watch the Live Stage with my child?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Children aged 4 years old through high school must have both a valid admission ticket for the applicable day and a Live Stage ticket to access the Live Stage. For safety reasons, children 3 years old and younger are not permitted to enter the Live Stage venue (B1F Sumitomo Hall). Thank you for your understanding.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I enter the venue with a stroller?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Yes, strollers are allowed inside the venue. However, there is no dedicated stroller parking area, so please manage your stroller and belongings at your own responsibility. Please note that the venue is expected to be crowded, so take extra care to avoid contact with other guests during busy periods.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

How do I get to the venue?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

The event will be held at Shinjuku Sumitomo Building Sankaku Hiroba (2-6-1 Nishi-Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo). The venue is directly connected to Toei Oedo Line Tochomae Station, a 4-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line Nishi-Shinjuku Station, and an 8-minute walk from Shinjuku Station (JR Lines and other lines).

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I bring food and drinks into the venue?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

We kindly ask that you refrain from bringing food or drinks into the venue. However, this does not apply to guests with food allergies or infants’ meals. Please note that eating and drinking are strictly prohibited inside B1F Sumitomo Hall (Live Stage).

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Can I take photos or videos at the venue?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Photography and video recording are permitted in the 1F Main Area. However, please be considerate of other guests, as they may unintentionally appear in photos or videos. Depending on the situation, venue staff may ask you to stop recording. Please note that photography, video recording, and audio recording are strictly prohibited inside the Live Stage venue (B1F Sumitomo Hall).

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Are pets allowed at the venue?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

Pets are not permitted inside the venue, except for guide dogs, assistance dogs, and hearing assistance dogs.

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/019.webp)

Will the event be held in case of severe weather?

![](https://assets.atmos-tokyo.com/assets/img/features/atmos-con_2026/020.webp)

As the event will be held at an indoor venue, it is expected to proceed as scheduled in principle. However, the event may be canceled or the content may be changed due to natural disasters or other unavoidable circumstances. The latest updates will be announced on the official website and official social media channels.

"atmoscon" is a sneaker convention first held in Harajuku in  
2016 by atmos, the Tokyo-born sneaker retailer known worldwide.  
What started as a core event drawing just 600 attendees at vol.1  
has since grown in scale, riding the rise of street culture and sneaker fandom.  
  
Last year, atmos celebrated its 25th anniversary — and after a hiatus during the pandemic,  
the convention made its long-awaited comeback, drawing its largest crowd yet.

atmoscon now embraces a wider range of culture, from music and food to sports and art,  
charting a new course toward becoming Asia's premier culture convention.

Whether you're already planning to enjoy the Sunday shows or your weekend plans are still being finalized, please take advantage of this opportunity to come and join us! Tickets will only be sold at the venue on the day of the event. Payment is by cash only, so please bring cash with you when you arrive. We look forward to seeing you on Sunday as well! \[Sunday-only day trip tickets\] Sunday 4: Admission ticket + day trip parking ticket 4000 yen Sunday 4: Admission ticket 3000 yen Check-in: 8:30 AM - 11:00 AM Check-out: 8:30 AM - 2:00 PM • Sales location: GO OUT CAMP vol.22 day-trip parking lot reception • Sales method: On-site sales only • Payment method: Cash only \*Tickets will not be sold through ticket agencies. The total amount of donations we received from everyone was 69,657 yen. We are pleased to report that all of the donations we received have been donated to the "2026 Kumamoto Earthquake Relief Fund (Kumamoto Prefecture)" implemented by Kumamoto Prefecture. We would like to express our sincere gratitude once again to everyone who cooperated and participated in each of the events, including the donations at the venue, the charity handheld fireworks, and the charity lottery. For more information about where your donation will go, please click here. [Regarding the acceptance of donations for the 2026 Kumamoto Earthquake](https://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/soshiki/27/274572.html) We would greatly appreciate your support through this donation. Please note that donation boxes are also available at the information desk. We would appreciate your cooperation even if you are not participating in the handheld fireworks event. If you wish to purchase a ticket on the day, please purchase it at the entrance on site. Please note that sales will end once tickets are sold out. ■Same-day ticket prices: 1-night/2-day admission ticket + auto camp parking ticket ¥11,000 2 \-night/3-day admission ticket + auto camp parking ticket ¥13,000 1-night/2-day admission ticket ¥7,500 2-night/3-day admission ticket ¥9,500 1-day (Saturday) day trip admission ticket + Saturday return parking ticket ¥4,000 1-day (Saturday) day trip admission ticket ¥2,500 **\*Please note that we only accept cash payments.** You can also enjoy the annual fireworks display over the water with a day-trip ticket!! We look forward to seeing you all! Sports drinks and beverages containing salt are also recommended. Please avoid direct sunlight by using a hat, parasol, towel, etc. Especially if you are with children, please have them wear hats or use sunshades on strollers. Dress in cool clothing and take breaks. Wear breathable clothing and take frequent breaks under a tarp or in the shade. **If you are not feeling well, please do not push yourself and come to the emergency room as soon as possible.** ■ Consult us immediately if you experience any of these symptoms : Dizziness, lightheadedness Headache, nausea, excessive sweating Fatigue, feeling drowsy, etc. If you experience any of these symptoms, they could be early signs of heatstroke. Please inform medical assistance immediately. Remember to stay hydrated and take frequent breaks to enjoy GO OUT CAMP Inawashiro to the fullest! Try again later. | Options ▼ [![Close](https://www.google.com/images/cleardot.gif)](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/news/info-2023-17/# "Close") # [![GOOUT CAMP Kansai](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/themes/template/common/images/header_logo_kansai.png)](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/) * [TICKET](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/ticket) * [NEWS](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/news) * [ARTIST](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/artist) * [ARTIST](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/artist) * [TIME TABLE](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/timetable) * [AREA MAP](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/area) * [ACTIVITY](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/activity) * [BOOTH](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/booth) * [ACCESS](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/access) * [GUIDELINE](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/guideline) * [ABOUT](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/about) notice Timetable announced!! 2023.08.14 The long-awaited timetable for live stages and activities has been decided!! The lineup includes Hitomi Yaida, also known as "Yaiko," a pioneer of female guitarists; OGA from JAH WORKS, a member of Osaka's long-established reggae sound system JAH WORKS; ZENDAMAN, the most talked-about reverse-imported DJ; Michael Kaneko, whose outstanding songwriting and overwhelming performances have attracted attention and who also composes music for commercials, movies, and anime; and Hanagara Lantern, a music duo based in Osaka that challenges itself to express itself with the minimal lineup of just one guitar and two vocals. In addition, GO OUT CAMP Kansai's regular DJs, DJ KENZ1 and DJ TAKAGI, and guest DJ CM SMOOTH will liven up the night. [**See the list of artists here**](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/artist/) There are plenty of activities that parents and children can enjoy together. Try again later. | Options ▼ [![Close](https://www.google.com/images/cleardot.gif)](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/news/info-2023-16/# "Close") # [![GOOUT CAMP Kansai](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/themes/template/common/images/header_logo_kansai.png)](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/) * [TICKET](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/ticket) * [NEWS](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/news) * [ARTIST](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/artist) * [ARTIST](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/artist) * [TIME TABLE](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/timetable) * [AREA MAP](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/area) * [ACTIVITY](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/activity) * [BOOTH](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/booth) * [ACCESS](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/access) * [GUIDELINE](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/guideline) * [ABOUT](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/about) notice From shopping to activities and workshops, we'll give you a thorough look inside the venue!! 2023.07.27 ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/MAP2-1-1024x538.jpg) With just about a month to go until GO OUT CAMP Kansai, we've thoroughly explored the venue. From live music and shopping to various activities, GO OUT CAMP Kansai offers a full day of fun, even for day-trippers! ① GOOUT STAGE: ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/c1ded8ef8f615e2f478582e8f391fd61-e1690419273440.jpg) The main stage featuring artists such as Hitomi Yaida, ZENDAMAN, OGA from JAH WORKS, and Michael Kaneko. A karaoke competition will also be held on this stage, where you too can become a festival performer! Show off your singing talent and get the audience excited. [**See the artist list here.**](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/artist/) ② Brand Avenue ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/e39ca5f40ce5cad31964228e7a437903-e1690419252615.jpg) A shopping area lined with booths from various brands and manufacturers. You're sure to find items you're interested in, from camping gear and apparel to shoes and backpacks. You might even find some great deals on outlet items! ③ Workshops If ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/4ab26880640e61f182850270fc5cf5ce.jpg) you want to enjoy workshops, come here! From woodworking experiences where you can carve your own cutlery using specialized tools, to candle making where you can create original candles and enjoy a relaxing time in a tent at night, this is the place. See **[the workshop list here .](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/activity/)** ④ Food Area ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/71e1ee70446601603b8637026e3fabd4.jpg) A wide variety of food options are available, from popular local foods like curry, hamburgers, and coffee to festival staples. With such diverse menus, you can enjoy delicious meals even if you don't bring your own ingredients – one of the great things about festivals! **[See the food booth list here.](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/booth/)** ⑤ DJ STAGE & Hiyoshi Yokocho ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/db77233e9bc8c391bf96ee71d31dcbf3.jpg) Next to the DJ STAGE, where you can enjoy the night of GO OUT CAMP with selections from DJ KENZ1, DJ TAKAGI, and others, the standing bar area "Hiyoshi Yokocho" will make its debut. Listen to the music, drink delicious alcohol, and have fun with fellow campers you meet there. ⑥ Market Village A ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/9772d53757144271b84cb3f2c332d3df.jpg) shopping area featuring a wide array of attractive, handcrafted goods, primarily from garage brands. You might find rare items or one-of-a-kind pieces that you wouldn't see in outdoor shops. Click **[here for a list of Market Village locations.](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/booth/)** ⑦ Activity & Kids Area ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/0e24b602c8e7d29a6cadf64720e1454d.jpg) Events include a sports day where people who meet for the first time form impromptu teams and compete seriously, a high-energy water fight where participants simply splash water on each other, and workshops for children in the kids area. See **[the activity list here.](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/activity/)** ⑧ Bouldering & Slackline: ![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/e554451edaa194eee7d06434b88bee96.jpg)![](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/61305bcf44e6968848620cf72eea2d6b.jpg) The bouldering wall produced by BOLD offers a unique experience with different difficulty levels depending on the angle of its four sides. A slackline park produced by EXALER Slackline Professionals, where you can try it for just 500 yen, is also available. **[Bouldering](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/activity/bouldering-3/)** **[Slackline](http://www.gooutcamp.jp/kansai/activity/slackline-2/)** This time, the gifts include Nissin's "Curry Meshi," LUVCA's "Leave-in Hair Care Products," and Care me's "Shampoo & Treatment." We are offering a highly practical lineup that will be useful during the event! Since it will be on a first-come, first-served basis, please come early if you are interested. ![](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/jamboree/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dadbec47f0d2ec5b989a4cf7f4e46679-e1775742888696.jpg) ![](https://www.gooutcamp.jp/jamboree/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/luvca2_sikyouhin_260305_ol-02-e1775742918542.jpg) ■ Nissin "Curry Meshi" This cup-type rice food that can be prepared with hot water is widely recognized and is popular for outdoor activities due to its convenience. It's a great option for a quick meal after arriving at a venue or as a snack in the evening. [https://www.currymeshi.com/](https://www.currymeshi.com/) ■LUVCA Leave-in Hair Care Products At outdoor events, hair tends to become dry and frizzy due to wind and dryness. Leave-in hair care products are a convenient way to keep your hair in good condition. With a non-greasy, smooth texture, it also helps to prevent bedhead the next morning. [https://www.hoyu.co.jp/luvca/](https://www.hoyu.co.jp/luvca/) ■Care me Shampoo & Treatment This shampoo and treatment set envelops you in natural fragrances, creating a relaxing time at the end of the day. It's also a great item to use during bath time after a day of fun at festivals or camping. [https://www.hoyu.co.jp/product/distribution/care-me/](https://www.hoyu.co.jp/product/distribution/care-me/)
